articles.title: David Raya's shot-stopping, cross-claiming and passing make him Premier League's best goalkeeper - The Radar
articles.summary: David Raya is the focus of The Radar column as he nears a new Arsenal contract. Plus, the numbers showing Newcastle's pressing problems under new head coach Matthias Jaissle. Watch Newcastle vs Arsenal live on Sky Sports on Saturday; kick-off 5.30pm
articles.body:
Welcome to The Radar , a Sky Sports column in which Nick Wright uses a blend of data and opinion to shed light on need-to-know Premier League stories. This week:

🔺Why Raya is the Premier League's best 🔺Newcastle's counter-pressing problem 🔺A player to watch this weekend

Unai Simon was named goalkeeper of the year at the Ballon d'Or ceremony but the 20,000 professional players who vote on the FIFPRO World XI went for David Raya. In fact, his total of 10,278 votes was the highest of any player - goalkeeper or otherwise.

Raya had to settle for a supporting role during Spain's World Cup campaign. Simon started every game and remains Luis de la Fuente's first choice in the position. But Raya's FIFPRO vote share reflected his status in the eyes of his fellow players.

Arsenal see him in the same way. Their new contract for Raya will reflect his standing as one of the world's best; recognition of his vital role in last season's Premier League title win and reward for how he has flourished since joining from Brentford in 2023.

Raya is now a three-time Golden Glove winner who has kept clean sheets in nearly half of his 117 Premier League appearances for Arsenal. He has an even better success rate in the Champions League, with 21 shutouts in 40 games in the same timeframe.

The numbers are extraordinary. But clean sheets are of course a collective endeavour. A deeper look into the data is required to build a true picture of Raya's individual excellence.

Gradient Sports , who grade players out of 100 based on the quality of their execution, rather than just the volume of their actions, have Raya as the Premier League's best or second-best performing 'keeper for a third straight season, reflecting his consistency.

Their goalkeeper grading system factors a broad range of performance elements, including, of course, the art of shot-stopping, one of many areas in which Raya continues to shine.

According to Gradient , who also grade shot quality, Raya is the only goalkeeper in the Premier League this season yet to concede a 'saveable' goal. For context, the data shows Emiliano Martinez, Alisson Becker and Gianluigi Donnarumma have conceded three, four and five respectively.

This is not just a statistical quirk, either. Since the start of last season, Raya's total of only six saveable goals conceded equates to just 0.13 per 90 minutes, the lowest rate of any goalkeeper to have played at least 20 per cent of available Premier League minutes.

Raya's reflexes are key to his shot-stopping. The quality of his positioning is another factor. According to Gradient's analysts, he hasn't made a single positional error when facing a shot this season.

Raya is of course well protected. Arsenal have the best defence in the Premier League and maybe Europe. But those defenders benefit from Raya's presence as much as he benefits from theirs.

When interviewing him for Sky Sports in 2024 , Raya highlighted the importance of another of his best attributes: his ability to claim crosses, which he credited to Iñaki Caña, the goalkeeping coach who followed him from Brentford to Arsenal.

"If you watch highlights from me when I was back at Blackburn, you will see a 'keeper that just stood on the line, not coming for anything, rarely going for a cross, rarely going outside the box, rarely anticipating, just waiting to make that save," he said.

"When I signed for Brentford, Iñaki just completely changed my style of being a goalkeeper, to be more proactive and anticipate stuff that has not happened yet. So, if you can go for a cross, just go for it. Don't wait for the save. Instead, avoid the chance."

Brentford fans will recall him being caught off his line by Joe Byram's long-range free-kick in the 2020 Championship play-off final. Arsenal fans will remember him failing to reach a high ball before Brian Brobbey's 94th-minute equaliser away to Sunderland.

But the rewards comfortably outweigh the risks overall.

This season, Gradient's data for crosses caught, factoring crosses caught at waist height or above, shows him top among goalkeepers, with 13. And that despite facing roughly 20 per cent fewer crosses than the two goalkeepers closest to his total.

Raya's dominance from crosses acts as a pressure release valve for Arsenal when defending their box. His efforts this season help to explain why the Gunners have one of the lowest opponent cross completion rates among Premier League sides.

Raya is shorter than the average goalkeeper at 6ft 1in, instead relying on his spring and athleticism when commanding his box. In possession, meanwhile, he benefits from vision that once prompted Jurgen Klopp to say he "should have number 10 on his back".

According to Gradient , Raya has completed the joint-most line-breaking passes of Premier League goalkeepers with this season. His total of 33 puts him level with Aston Villa's Zion Suzuki but with a higher success rate at 87 per cent to Suzuki's 79 per cent.

Suzuki stands out in the data as another goalkeeper who offers proactivity on crosses as well as progressive passing ability. But the Villa goalkeeper has conceded five saveable goals already this season, nearly as many as Raya in the last two combined.

It is that completeness, in shot-stopping, cross-claiming and distribution, that separates Raya from the rest in the Premier League. And while the Ballon d'Or voting went another way, it gives him a strong case to be considered one of the world's best too.

Arsenal next test comes at St James' Park, live on Sky Sports on Saturday, where Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle could really do with a result. He has only won one out of five Premier League home games since arriving from Saudi Arabian club Al Ahli.

Speaking to him while at Red Bull Salzburg , where he won back-to-back Austrian titles between 2021 and 2023, provided an insight into his philosophy. Jaissle is an advocate of quick, vertical attacks. But what came across most strongly was the overarching importance he places on out-of-possession work.

"The mentality is important, to see the nature of the player," Jaissle told Sky Sports . "Does he really want to chase the ball, to win it back? We also have a saying that mentality eats talent."

Jaissle likes to his teams to channel their intensity into Jurgen Klopp-like counter-pressing, which is defined as attempting to win the ball back within a few seconds of losing it. The idea is to capitalise on an opponent's disorganisation in the moments after regaining the ball, ideally high up the pitch.

Jaissle's Red Bull Salzburg excelled on this front. In their 2021/22 and 2022/23 Champions League campaigns, they ranked ninth and seventh respectively among the 32 competing sides for possessions won in the final third per game. But his Newcastle players have so far struggled to make the same tactics work.

According to Opta, Newcastle sit 17th among Premier League sides for high-intensity counter pressures this season.

Brighton, Arsenal and Manchester City, the Premier League's top three, also feature low on the list. But that is largely because they dominate the ball, averaging roughly 60 per cent possession, meaning there are fewer opportunities to counter-press. Newcastle, by contrast, only average 50 per cent possession.

Counter-pressure locations provides further evidence of Newcastle's struggles. While Brighton. City and Arsenal rank among the sides with the highest percentages of counter-pressures in the final third, Newcastle sit among the lowest.

Their share of just 36 per cent in the final third, compared 56 per cent in the middle third and eight per cent in the defensive third, means they are counter-pressing in less dangerous areas as well as less than most of their rivals overall.

For Jaissle, the issues are compounded by structural problems which have given opponents space to attack when Newcastle's attempts to press are unsuccessful, as shown by their Premier League-high total of 20 shots faced from fast breaks this term.

Expect Arsenal to be set up to capitalise.

Player Radar: Who else to keep an eye on

After a difficult season in front of goal last term, Evanilson is becoming yet another Bournemouth success story. He faces Nottingham Forest on Saturday having scored, assisted, or done both, in seven of his last eight games in all competitions.

Four Premier League games are live on Sky Sports this weekend, starting when Newcastle host Arsenal at 5.30pm on Saturday.

Sunday sees Hull City take on Brighton at 2pm, before Liverpool face Man Utd in Mauricio Pochettino's first game at 4.30pm.

Lastly, Brentford face Everton on Monday Night Football at 8pm. Watch coverage with David Jones and Co from 6.30pm.

Last week's column made the case for Estevao to play more minutes for Chelsea and highlighted Brighton's incredible physical intensity, summed up by Pascal Gross , in their win over Liverpool.

articles.title: Gol impede cadela com câncer de viajar para receber tratamento em SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Stella, de 9 anos, fez cirurgia para remover tumor no focinho e precisa de radioterapia. Juíza chegou a obrigar companhia a garantir viagem, mas empresa recorreu e decisão foi anulada.
articles.summary: Stella, de 9 anos, fez cirurgia para remoção de tumor no focinho e precisa de radioterapia. Companhia aérea recusou transporte do animal na cabine de passageiros.
articles.body:
Os tutores de uma cadela da raça Golden Retriever processaram a Gol Linhas Aéreas na Justiça para conseguir viajar de avião com o animal na cabine de passageiros ( veja vídeo acima ). A cachorra Stella, de 9 anos, tem carcinoma nasal, um câncer considerado agressivo. Ela passou por uma cirurgia no fim de outubro e precisa sair do Recife para realizar 12 sessões de radioterapia em São Paulo .

Por causa da condição de saúde dela, veterinários recomendaram que Stella viajasse acompanhada. No entanto, a companhia aérea negou o transporte por questões de segurança. A tutora Vera Melo e o filho dela, o advogado Márcio Melo, disseram que, sem a radioterapia, a expectativa de vida de Stella é de seis meses. Caso o tratamento seja feito, a cadela poderá viver por mais dois anos (saiba mais abaixo) .

Segundo os tutores, a viagem deve acontecer antes do dia 21 de novembro, quando começa o tratamento no outro estado. Márcio disse que, quando deu entrada no processo, apresentou certificados de que a cadela é adestrada, além de laudos do veterinário que recomendam o transporte do animal na cabine com os tutores.

"Eles [a Gol] alegam questão de segurança de bordo e impossibilidade técnica. Se é autorizado para o cão-guia, para o cão de suporte emocional, que é o mesmo porte, por que não seria autorizado? A gente iria comprar o assento, seria um assento para mim, para ela [Stella] e para minha mãe. Ela é adestrada. Juntei o comprovante de adestramento, fiz vários vídeos, mostrei que ela atende a todos os comandos. Então, questão de perturbação de bordo não teria nenhuma. A única diferença realmente para cão-guia é que ela não tem o treinamento para guiar, de fato", explicou.

Vera contou que foi duas vezes com o filho ao Aeroporto Internacional do Recife, na Zona Sul da cidade, para tentar a autorização da Gol e comprar as passagens. A primeira foi no domingo (15) e depois na segunda-feira (16), quando passaram horas aguardando o atendimento.

"Passamos seis horas em frente a um café, que fica na frente da Gol. As pessoas lá, as atendentes, ficaram impressionadas como Stella ficou deitada as seis horas. Ela só se levantou quando peguei ela e fui lá fora para ela fazer as necessidades. Inclusive, tinha gente que dizia: 'meu Deus, ela já teria ido para São Paulo e voltado, e não saiu do canto'", contou.

No dia 17 de novembro, a juíza Luciana Ferreira de Araújo Magalhães, do 15º Juizado Especial Cível das Relações de Consumo da Capital, concedeu uma liminar obrigando a empresa a autorizar o embarque de Stella.

Porém, no mesmo dia, a Gol teve um mandado de segurança aprovado pela 2ª Turma Recursal do 1º Colégio Recursal da Capital. Com isso, a decisão da juíza foi suspensa e a companhia aérea não é mais obrigada a fazer o transporte da cadela.

De acordo com resolução da Anac, o transporte de animais de estimação e animais de suporte emocional pelas companhias aéreas não é obrigatório. As empresas aéreas que optarem por oferecer o serviço podem avaliar se há risco à segurança das operações aéreas.

Como a data para início do tratamento se aproxima, Vera e Marcio procuram outras opções de companhias aéreas.

"A Latam viu a situação e estava tentando resolver, mas disse que 'por regimento interno, realmente, questão da companhia, a gente precisa liminar. Com a liminar, a gente emite passagem, a gente faz tudo aqui'. [...] Eu estou em contato com a Azul para ver se a gente consegue alguma coisa de forma administrativa", disse o advogado.

Cadela Stella aguarda permissão para embarcar em voo do Recife para São Paulo — Foto: Reprodução/WhatsApp

De acordo com os tutores, as sessões de radioterapia devem começar na próxima semana para garantir a eficácia do tratamento, que deve durar cerca de um mês.

"Ela está na janela de oportunidade muito boa. Justamente por a cirurgia de remoção ser muito agressiva, se ela já passou dessa fase, a radioterapia vai ter um efeito muito bom, porque vai agir direto nas células [de câncer] que ficaram", disse Márcio Melo.

Vera Melo compartilhou com o g1 um vídeo gravado pela veterinária de Stella, Andrea Cruz. No comunicado, a profissional afirma que não é ideal atrasar o início do tratamento e que a cadela não pode ser transportada para outro estado sem condições adequadas.

"Quanto mais tempo passa, mais aumenta a possibilidade de Stella ter uma rescindiva dessa massa tumoral. [...] Merece respeito e merece um transporte de segurança. Um animal que tem um distúrbio de via aérea jamais poderá ser colocado em uma caixa de transporte e jogado na carga de um avião", declara a veterinária no vídeo.

"os critérios de peso, dimensões e acondicionamento estão respaldados pela regulamentação da Anac [Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil] e pelo entendimento do STJ, que reconhece a possibilidade de as companhias aéreas estabelecerem condições para o transporte de animais de estimação";

"na aviação comercial, o transporte na cabine de animais de médio ou grande porte fora de recipientes apropriados, ressalvado o regime legal específico dos cães-guia, apresenta riscos à segurança operacional, como a obstrução de corredores, dificuldades em procedimentos de evacuação e a utilização de dispositivos de contenção sem comprovação de compatibilidade técnica com as aeronaves";

"reforça seu respeito e empatia por todos os clientes e seus animais de estimação, mas reafirma que a Segurança é seu valor número 1 e inegociável".

A companhia aérea informou que as situações são avaliadas individualmente e, no caso de Stella, que é um animal de estimação de médio a grande porte, não há alternativas para o transporte. Desde 2024, a Gol proibiu o transporte de pets no porão de suas aeronaves .

articles.title: Infantino remains favourite as FIFA president gets two challengers for 2027 vote
articles.summary: FIFA president Gianni Infantino will face his first contested re-election battle since 2023, with French Football Federation (FFF) president Philippe
articles.body: FIFA president Gianni Infantino will face his first contested re-election battle since 2023, with French Football Federation (FFF) president Philippe Diallo and Japan's Kozo Tashima emerging as challengers for the top job at world football's governing body.Both candidates submitted their nominations ahead of the midnight deadline in Zurich, with letters of support from five member federations, FIFA confirmed on Thursday. The election involving FIFA's 211 member associations is scheduled for March 18, 2027, in Rabat, Morocco.Infantino, who has led FIFA since 2016, was re-elected unopposed in 2023. He is now seeking another four-year term, which would keep him in office until 2031 and take his presidency to 15 years."The candidatures have been forwarded to the electoral committee for examination and for passing a decision on the admission of the candidates," FIFA said in a statement.The governing body added: "Member associations will be notified of the names of the proposed and admitted candidates no later than 18 February 2027."UEFA-backed Diallo emerges as key challengerDiallo announced his candidacy on Monday with the backing of UEFA member associations represented on its executive committee and the FIFA Council. He took over as FFF president in 2023 and played a leading role in the European opposition to Infantino's FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal.Tashima had declared his intention to contest the election earlier this month and formally submitted his nomination on Wednesday.The FFE proposal, which sought to sell private investors stakes in the profits of the World Cup and other major competitions, triggered a fierce backlash after it was revealed in July. Infantino eventually dropped the plan."Against the backdrop of serious concerns over the direction of FIFA, the national associations called for renewed unity and trust within the global football community," UEFA said on Monday.Infantino remains favourite despite eligibility questionsDespite repeated calls for his resignation, Infantino is widely seen as the favourite, with many of FIFA's member associations outside Europe appearing satisfied with his leadership. He has directed significant funding towards national federations and promised an additional $25 million to each through 2030.However, his bid for another term could face scrutiny over FIFA's presidential term limits. The statutes allow three full terms, but FIFA's legal advice in 2022 held that Infantino's initial 2016-19 stint, when he completed Sepp Blatter's unfinished mandate, did not count towards the limit.Candidates must also pass eligibility and integrity checks by FIFA's three-member electoral panel, whose decisions can be challenged at the Court of Arbitration for Sport.The final list of approved candidates is due by February 18, 2027.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jhon Perlaza: Ecuadorian footballer given eight-year ban for throwing stone at assistant referee
articles.summary: Ecuadorian footballer Jhon Perlaza is banned for eight years after hitting an assistant referee with a rock during a third-tier match.
articles.body:
An Ecuadorian footballer has been banned for eight years for throwing a rock at an assistant referee, leaving him requiring surgery to his face.

Jhon Perlaza was playing for Club Ciudad de Yantzaza against Club Rio Aguarico FC in a third-tier match in October when the incident took place.

The stone struck assistant referee Lenin Giovanni Ojeda Nunez in the face in the 96th minute of the game, which was subsequently abandoned.

A video on social media shows Perlaza standing up in the team's dugout to throw the stone, with Nunez instantly falling to the floor and holding his face after the object hits him. He then receives medical attention.

"The assistant referee suffered serious injuries that required surgery and a 60-day recovery period," the Ecuadorian Football Federation (FEF) said.

"The disciplinary committee found the player responsible for physical aggression against a match official and suspended him for eight years from all football-related activity, until 19 October, 2034.

"In addition, the FEF will ask Fifa to extend this sanction worldwide."

The FEF also fined his club Yantzaza $2,000 (£1,521) and ordered them to pay Nunez's medical fees of $4,369 (£3,323).

In a statement released on 20 October, three days after the match, Yantzaza apologised to the refereeing team and the fans, and confirmed Perlaza had been sacked as a result of the incident.

"As an institution, we categorically reject all acts of aggression, whether verbal or physical, both inside and outside sporting venues. We firmly believe that football should be a space of respect, coexistence, and fair play," they said.

"Once the person responsible for this regrettable incident was identified, the institution made the decision to remove him immediately, and he is therefore no longer part of our club."

articles.title: Vincent Kompany: Bayern Munich manager to return to dugout on Friday
articles.summary: Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompany says he is "very healthy" and grateful for all of the support he has recieved as he prepares to return to the dugout on Friday.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompany says he is "very healthy" and grateful for all of the support he has received as he prepares to return to the dugout on Friday.

The 40-year-old former Manchester City captain was taken to hospital after falling ill while watching the club's second team train last month.

Kompany was diagnosed with meningeal irritation - an inflammation of the protective membrane surrounding the brain and spinal cord.

Speaking at a news conference on Thursday he thanked the club, medical staff, players, coaches and fans for their support.

"At the time, it was a new experience. Looking back, everything went perfectly. I received support right away, from the club and the doctors. I'm very grateful.

"You try to stay calm and wait until you have the results. It was a positive process, all the tests were positive.

"I have to say, I'm very healthy. We did a lot of tests, and they all came back fine. In those quiet moments, you also try to learn.

"Now I feel very good again and I'm happy to be back with the team."

While he has been recovering Kompany's assistant Aaron Danks has led the side to four wins and a draw.

"I'd also like to thank the coaching community," Kompany added. "We're always competing, but almost every coach has reached out to me, even if we've played against each other and perhaps argued as well. That's a beautiful thing."

Bayern, for whom England captain Harry Kane has been in fine form, are top of the Bundesliga, level on points with Borussia Dortmund.

Defending champions Bayern face Cologne on Friday after the end of the two-week international break.

articles.title: El mercado que viene: Rüdiger, Nico Paz, Kovacic, De Bruyne, Brahim...
articles.standfirst: Matteo Moretto analiza en La Pizarra de Quintana los nombres a seguir
articles.summary: Matteo Moretto analiza en La Pizarra de Quintana los nombres a seguir
articles.body: El futuro de Antonio Rüdiger en el Real Madrid sigue siendo una incógnita. El central alemán es uno de los futbolistas cuya continuidad está pendiente de resolverse y su situación podría ser diferente a la de otros compañeros que ya han ampliado sus contratos. Matteo Moretto ha analizado en La Pizarra de Quintana, de Radio MARCA, junto a Miguel Quintana, Adrián Blanco y Nahuel Miranda, las principales operaciones del mercado, con especial atención a los jugadores que terminan contrato el próximo 30 de junio de 2027. Sobre Rüdiger, el periodista italiano ha reconocido que existen dudas acerca de su continuidad en el conjunto blanco. "Yo creo que el club lo va a valorar, que lo va a hablar de manera directa con Rüdiger entre marzo y abril", ha explicado. Moretto no ha querido dar por segura su salida, aunque ha dejado abierta esa posibilidad: "No te quiero decir que esté fuera al 100%. Tene pinta... pero aún no está decidido al 100%". El periodista ha señalado que el liderazgo del alemán y su estado físico serán factores importantes en la decisión. Otro de los nombres propios ha sido Nico Paz, que continúa destacando en el Como de Cesc Fàbregas. Moretto considera que el Real Madrid sigue muy pendiente de su evolución y que será uno de los grandes protagonistas del próximo mercado de verano. "Yo sé que el Madrid sigue muy atento", ha asegurado. El periodista también ha destacado el crecimiento del argentino y ha dejado clara su opinión sobre una posible vuelta al Santiago Bernabéu: "Yo te diría que veo súper extraño si el Madrid pierde el control sobre él. A lo mejor el Madrid lo puede fichar otra vez de vuelta para luego ver qué pasa". En cuanto a Brahim Díaz, Moretto ha confirmado que su situación contractual está resuelta, al igual que la de Thibaut Courtois. "Tanto Brahim Díaz como Courtois han renovado. Los dos ya tienen un contrato firmado y ampliado", ha explicado. Sin embargo, el periodista considera que habrá que seguir de cerca los minutos del internacional marroquí: "Yo sé que quiere jugar un poquito más". Una de las informaciones más llamativas de la sección ha sido la posible salida de Kevin De Bruyne del Nápoles rumbo al PSV Eindhoven. Moretto ha revelado que el futbolista ya habría dado el visto bueno a la operación: "La información que tengo es que Kevin De Bruyne ya ha dicho que sí al PSV. Hay una negociación en marcha entre los clubes: el PSV ya ha presentado una oferta, alrededor de los dos kilos, y el Nápoles pide más". Pese a las diferencias económicas, el periodista ha señalado que existe buena sintonía entre las partes. "Por un tema familiar, Kevin De Bruyne acabaría en el PSV", ha añadido. También ha hablado de Mateo Kovacic, cuyo futuro podría estar lejos del Manchester City. "A final de temporada se va a despedir del City", ha asegurado Moretto, que ha explicado que el centrocampista ya tuvo opciones de salir el pasado verano. Italia aparece como uno de sus posibles destinos, aunque el periodista tampoco descarta España: "Le apetecería volver a España o volver a Italia, pero esto depende también del salario que pide". En el fútbol español, Moretto ha puesto el foco en Marc Aguado, cuyo contrato con el Elche termina al final de la temporada. El periodista ha revelado que el Espanyol ya está dando pasos para intentar su incorporación: "Ya hay un club que está preguntando y que se está moviendo... y es el Espanyol". Por otro lado, el futuro de Borja Mayoral en el Getafe también podría resolverse en los próximos meses. Moretto considera que el delantero tiene muchas posibilidades de abandonar el conjunto azulón: "Entre enero y junio, dejará el Getafe. No está teniendo protagonismo, no está teniendo minutos, tiene un salario muy alto...". Aunque todavía desconoce cuál podría ser su próximo destino, el periodista ha insistido en que el club madrileño ya contempla la necesidad de reforzar su delantera: "Yo creo que el Getafe ya sabe que tiene que buscar otro delantero más". La sección también ha dejado novedades sobre otros futbolistas de LaLiga. En el caso de Álex Remiro, Moretto ha explicado que la Real Sociedad le ha presentado una propuesta para continuar, aunque las negociaciones todavía no han llegado a buen puerto. "Remiro tiene una oferta a la baja por parte de la Real Sociedad. Las partes llevan negociando semanas, incluso meses", ha revelado. También ha señalado el interés de clubes españoles, italianos e ingleses por el guardameta. Una situación similar atraviesa Sergi Cardona, que todavía no ha alcanzado un acuerdo para renovar con el Villarreal y por el que ya ha preguntado el Atlético de Madrid. Más contundente se ha mostrado con Sergio Camello, delantero del Rayo Vallecano. "Para mí va a salir sí o sí. No hay acuerdo, tampoco hay oferta sobre la mesa", ha afirmado. Moretto ha confirmado que clubes como el Como y el Marsella, además de equipos de LaLiga, ya han trasladado propuestas verbales a su entorno.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino at Manchester United: New boss vows to change situation at Old Trafford in first interview
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino has vowed to "change things" at Manchester United; the Argentine insists his immediate priority is unlocking the potential of the existing squad and creating a culture capable of bringing success back to Old Trafford
articles.body:
In a sit-down with United's social channels, Pochettino revealed:

His ambitions to change the current situation at Old Trafford

The need to show love to the Manchester United squad

Backing from the Manchester United hierarchy

Planning ahead of Sunday's Liverpool trip

The Argentine arrived at Old Trafford following his departure from the United States national team, with the task of improving United's fortunes after their dismal start to the season. United sit 18th in the Premier League ahead of Pochettino's first game in charge, which will be Sunday's trip to Liverpool at Anfield, live on Sky Sports .

Pochettino believes it would be a mistake to focus solely on United's current predicament, insisting the club's potential, rather than its problems, must be the starting point for his tenure.

"It's a mistake to see the situation. We need to see the potential of this club," he said in his first interview as United head coach.

"It's about to start to act and to change things, and to try to affect in a good way all the areas, to try to really believe that we can recover that feeling about to win."

Pochettino has little time to settle in, but insists his priority is to create an environment in which United's players can express themselves and rediscover the feeling of winning.

"The most important thing is for us to start to work hard to recover that feeling. That feeling is about being winners, to win games, to perform. But that is not only to talk about winning."

Pochettino: We need to love the players we have

The club are targeting a left-back, centre-back and forward as areas to potentially strengthen. Pochettino is expected to have input on targets they will pursue.

However, with just over a month to go until the transfer window does open, Pochettino has emphasised how his main priority lies with getting the best out of the current squad at his disposal, as he looks to rectify the dismal start to the season.

United have 10 fixtures across all competitions before they will be able to add reinforcements in the New Year.

"The best request that we can have, the players that we have, and we need to love the players that we have," Pochettino added. "We need to support the players, we need to provide all the tools for their performance.

"It's only an act of responsibility now to start to work and provide them the possibility to translate all their talent on the field."

Pochettino insists he has backing from Man Utd hierarchy

Pochettino also insisted he has the full support of United's hierarchy, despite growing tensions between the club's leadership, players and supporters.

The relationship between the board and sections of the fanbase has been strained by protests against the Glazer family and minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, with supporters voicing their frustration over the club's direction, transfer strategy and investment.

There has also been public discontent from within the dressing room, with Lisandro Martinez directly criticising director of football Jason Wilcox following United's Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid in October.

The defender questioned the club's summer recruitment and said he expected more from "upstairs", specifically naming Wilcox before later apologising following talks with the club's leadership and Carrick.

Asked about the support he has received from senior figures since his arrival, Pochettino was unequivocal.

"I feel all the support. We feel all the support from the director and the owner," he said.

"And of course, now it's up to us to provide what they expect from us.

"We have a clear idea of what the club expects from us, and we want to be at the level of the demand of this football club."

Pochettino also stressed the importance of creating unity across all areas of the club, including the relationship between the hierarchy, players, coaching staff and supporters.

"We need to be united. Because in the end, we are Manchester United," he said.

Pochettino: We will go to Anfield with the idea to win

Pochettino's first assignment will be a daunting one, with United travelling to face Liverpool on Sunday, but he insists his side will approach the game with ambition.

"We are going to go there, to Anfield, with the idea to win and be brave and to be Manchester United," he said.

"We need to make sure that we are brave and we are protagonists, and go there with no fears and challenge a very good team like Liverpool."

Pochettino also insisted it is the responsibility of his team to reconnect with supporters rather than place further demands on them.

"I'm not going to ask nothing because I think always we demand, demand, demand to the fans, but we need to provide to the fans before to the man," he said.

"The fans need to see that we are going to fight, you know, we are Manchester United and we respect our history and we are going to play for a win."

He added: "We are going to work so hard for you to feel proud about the team, the players and, of course, that is the most important, the club."

articles.title: Chelsea: Ten things we've learnt about Xabi Alonso's Blues after 10 Premier League games
articles.summary: From a battle to be No 1 and various midfield combinations to set-pieces and systems, there's plenty to pick out from Xabi Alonso's start at Chelsea; Here we examine 10 takeaways so far; Follow Chelsea vs Leeds on Saturday with our live blog on the Sky Sports website and App, kick-off 3pm
articles.body:
1 - Could Mike Penders become the preferred option to No 1 Emi Martinez?

Goalkeeper has been a long-standing problem position at Chelsea. Xabi Alonso spoke positively about his keeping options after taking charge but a night to forget for Robert Sanchez at Fulham in the Spaniard's first game in charge pushed the club into action. The 2022 World Cup winner Emiliano Martinez seemed like a no-brainer. However, the 34-year-old let three goals in on his debut against Brighton and hasn't looked totally assured.

An injury to the Argentine has created an opportunity for the highly rated Mike Penders. A calamitous own goal for the 21-year-old against Spurs was a terrible way to mark his first Premier League start but his response has been impressive. It is food for thought that Penders has a positive Expected Goals Against vs Actual Goals Conceded ratio (4.49 vs only three let in). Martinez's return is negative - 11 goals conceded from shots worth 9.17.

Petr Cech was just 22 when he made his Chelsea debut and went on to achieve legendary status. Alonso evidently didn't believe the Belgian international was ready at the start of this campaign but Penders has certainly given his manager something to consider.

2 - Inconsistent Chelsea's longest winning streak in the Premier League so far

Chelsea have been consistently inconsistent so far. They bounced back from a poor draw with Hull and even worse thumping at Brentford by dishing out a 5-1 thrashing of Bournemouth, while losses to Spurs and Sunderland have tempered expectations. Three games in, their trip to the Emirates was billed as an opportunity to show they could be a real threat - potentially even title contenders. Instead, after 10 games, they're 11 points behind Arsenal and unlikely to trouble the Premier League champions.

They've won back-to-back league games just twice and have yet to demonstrate evidence of a clear identity forming. Injuries to key personnel have hampered Alonso. The Chelsea boss has continually stated his side will look different in May, compared to what we are witnessing now. However, the journey and the eventual destination isn't obvious. Yet in spite of four league defeats already, the Blues are relatively well-placed for Champions League qualification.

3 - Games in a row without a recognised striker

We'll come onto Joao Pedro's brilliant start but Alonso's curious approach to his recent injury issue has sparked debate. Chelsea started without a recognised striker against Spurs, Man Utd and Sunderland, with Danny Welbeck given just a few minutes off the bench in the first two of those games before going on after an hour as Chelsea chased an equaliser at the Stadium of Light. With summer signings Welbeck and Emmanuel Emegha not trusted and Liam Delap, Nicolas Jackson and Marc Guiu sold, Chelsea look short up front.

Morgan Rogers and Pedro Neto have been used as false nines. The former Aston Villa man offers a presence when deployed there but Neto's usage is difficult to comprehend. Welbeck has been ineffective in starts against Brentford and Liverpool in the cup but Chelsea lack a focal point without a natural forward. They also have the biggest positive difference between goals scored (19) and Expected Goals (15.9). While that is the result of some stunning strikes, it also raises questions about the long-term sustainability of their attacking threat after blanks against Tottenham and Sunderland.

In pre-season, there was much debate about whether Alonso would utilise the back-three set-up which served him so well at Bayer Leverkusen or go with a four as he did at Real Madrid. The answer is: a bit of both. There have been six matches when Chelsea have started with a four and four when they've gone with a three.

Alonso has been keen to stress that in-play shape is more significant than how the names are laid out in a graphic but his variations suggest he is still searching for the right formula - and Chelsea's inconsistent performances and results reflect that uncertainty. Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana have failed to convince at the start of this season and Maxence Lacroix is not injured. Academy graduate Josh Acheampong has been the only major positive defensively so far. He has mightily impressed.

5 - Times Chelsea have had more or less possession

Beyond formations, preconceptions about the style of play under Alonso have also been challenged in these opening 10 games. In half of them, Chelsea have had more possession than their opponents and bossed the ball. But it's been a different story in the other matches.

In fact, it was stunning to see Chelsea register just 26 per cent possession at home to Brighton in a game they won 4-3. They had just 31 per cent of the ball at home to Spurs. A performance which deeply frustrated the home support.

Part of the plan or a stat which speaks to deeper issues around controlling matches and winning midfield battles? Alonso has admitted that he wants his team to be better with the ball, a message he delivered at half-time to spark an upturn in performance against Manchester United.

Alonso was a midfield maestro in his playing days and he has made no secret of declaring the central area as key to his team's success. But he has tried six different midfield combinations so far. Moises Caicedo's early-season injury problem was unhelpful, as was the subsequent Reece James lay-off. Romeo Lavia has at least been fit and impressed, while Jordan Henderson seems to have struck up a relationship with Caicedo. All three started in the defeat at Sunderland. It remains, though, an area of debate.

The sale of Enzo Fernandez late in the transfer window without an adequate replacement coming in has proved to be a problem. A January priority?

7 - Goals from set-pieces and penalties - for and against!

Such is the modern game, transfers of set-piece coaches is now a thing, and Chelsea's capture of Aston Villa's Austin MacPhee - an A-lister in the category - this summer drew attention. The results so far are best described as mixed. Only Brighton have scored more than Chelsea's six from set-piece situations, before you add in Cole Palmer's penalty against Man Utd. But no side has conceded more than their six from set-pieces, with Enzo Le Fee's penalty for Sunderland making the dead-ball for/against tally level.

Their resilient display at Everton suggested progress had been made. However, Alonso, MacPhee and Chelsea have work to do if they are to master this important department at both ends of the pitch.

8 - Still the number of Chelsea goals scored by Estevao

With JP Morgan (are we sticking with that name for Chelsea's first-choice front three?) making a flying start to the season, the knock-on effect has been reduced opportunities for Estevao. In fact, Alonso's persistent reluctance to throw the teenage Brazilian into the action has become a frustrating issue for Chelsea supporters, given the electric winger is a firm fan favourite. Like fellow 19-year-old Geovany Quenda - who signed an eight-year contract in the summer - Estevao has made just one Premier League start so far.

The absence of European football hasn't helped, with Chelsea's number of matches reduced this term, and Estevao was out to prove a point when he was given his shot against Man Utd. Despite his best efforts, he was unable to add to the eight goals he scored last season. A narrow offside call prevented him from adding to his tally.

He returned to the bench for the defeat at Sunderland. It's a situation Alonso needs to manage. Estevao has been seen as "untouchable" and unavailable for sale. However, the situation seems unsustainable if the Brazilian spends more time warming the bench than racing up the touchline.

The Chelsea No 9 jersey has weighed heavy on its wearer for some time. From Radamel Falcao and Alvaro Morata a decade ago through to Romelu Lukaku, Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang and Liam Delap in more recent seasons, strikers have failed to repeat their prolificacy at other clubs when they've been marked out as Chelsea's main forward. But Joao Pedro has bucked the trend.

He has five goals and three assists in his six Premier League appearances so far and Chelsea's attack looks far better connected with him leading the line. Joao Pedro has emerged as perhaps Alonso's most important player. They need to keep him fit. Chelsea have scored just two goals in the four league matches he has missed - both coming in the win over United.

10 - Starts for in-form pair Palmer and Rogers

Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers are the only players to have started all 10 Chelsea Premier League games for Alonso.

Chelsea No 10 Palmer has shown glimpses of his best form and looks close to full fitness. He appears to have found his spark after his struggles last season, although his returns have been inconsistent. His three goals and three assists only tell part of the story. He looks a different player when he has Joao Pedro ahead of him. At times he has looked unplayable. Without the Brazilian striker, he has struggled to impact games as much. He let his frustration show with his sending-off against Spurs.

His status as an England international remains a major topic of debate. A small injury forced him to withdraw from Thomas Tuchel's squad in September. He appears to have fallen down Tuchel's pecking order as a result.

Palmer's good friend Rogers has fiercely defended his desire to play for England and on the pitch they have worked well in tandem, too.

articles.title: Northern Ireland: Striker Simone Magill returns to squad for Greece friendlies
articles.summary: Northern Ireland manager Michael McArdle has made five changes to his squad for the upcoming friendlies against Greece, with the return of experienced striker Simone Magill among the notable returnees.
articles.body:
Northern Ireland manager Michael McArdle has made five changes to his squad for the upcoming friendlies against Greece, with the return of experienced striker Simone Magill among the notable returnees.

Magill, who gave birth to her daughter Skye over the summer, returned to training with the Northern Ireland squad last month but did not play in either leg of the World Cup play-off defeat by Portugal.

The 32-year-old Birmingham City forward has not represented Northern Ireland since announcing her pregnancy just over a year ago and will now be hoping to add to her 95 caps and 28 international goals.

Glentoran midfielder Chloe McCarron returns after an injury-hit spell, while Hibernian's Joely Andrews is also back after missing the Portugal games through injury. Both featured for Northern Ireland at the Euros in 2022.

Kerry Beattie completes the trio of returnees in the 24-player squad after impressing in front of goal since joining Portsmouth from Aberdeen during the summer.

'You can be a mum and a footballer - they can co-exist'

Family, football and Dalglish - what drives NI boss McArdle?

There is also a senior recall for defender Ella Haughey. The 22-year-old West Brom player last received a call-up in 2021, when she was named among the substitutes for friendlies against England and Scotland.

Meanwhile, Kess Elmore, Jane McMaster and Lucy-Jayne Grant have retained their places after receiving their first senior call-ups last month.

Injured defender Natalie Johnson misses out, alongside Mia Moore, Naomi McLaughlin, Charlotte Havern and Leyla McFarland.

Both matches will take place at Inver Park in Larne, with the first meeting scheduled for Friday 27 November before the sides face off again on Tuesday 1 December.

Northern Ireland currently sit 52nd in the Fifa world rankings, six places above Greece.

Analysis - Magill's return a boost for the squad

The Birmingham City forward's return has been carefully managed through close collaboration between Northern Ireland and her club, with both parties keen to ensure she is given the time and support needed to make the transition back into competitive football.

Michael McArdle was delighted to welcome his captain back into the fold, revealing that Magill's family were also involved in the previous international camp as she began preparing for life as a mother and professional footballer.

"I'm delighted we've got our captain back," McArdle told BBC Sport NI.

"We've had on the last camp Simone, her husband Mark and Skye as well, just as a transition for us all to get ready for the future for Simone as a mother athlete now.

"That's the exciting piece for her, but great to have her back in a playing capacity now. No pressure or expectation for Simone. It's part of the process collaboratively between us and Birmingham."

Magill also had the opportunity to get back on the training pitch during the previous camp, taking another important step in her gradual return.

McArdle explained that considerable work has been taking place behind the scenes at Birmingham City, with the club's performance staff working closely alongside Northern Ireland's team to manage her progress.

"There's a lot of work going on at the club just now to support Simone's return," he said.

"This opportunity to be in camp and selected again is that opportunity to take that, hopefully playing minutes as well."

Although she has yet to make a public appearance for Birmingham this season, McArdle confirmed that Magill has continued working and gaining minutes behind closed doors.

"We've been very close with Birmingham since pre-season, so Birmingham's performance team and our performance team work together," he added.

For Northern Ireland, however, her return is about more than simply adding another player to the squad. Magill's experience, leadership and influence remain hugely important.

"Her presence, obviously, is our captain and our leader within the playing group, for us as staff as well," McArdle said.

With no expectations placed on her immediate playing involvement, the priority is ensuring Magill's comeback happens at the right pace, while allowing Northern Ireland to benefit from having their captain back among the group.

Goalkeepers: Jackie Burns (Burnley), Lauren Perry (Montrose), Maddy Harvey-Clifford (Cliftonville).

Defenders: Rebecca Holloway and Rebecca McKenna (both Birmingham City), Abi Sweetlove and Jane McMaster (both Linfield), Ellie Mason (Charlton), Fi Morgan (Celtic), Ella Haughey (West Bromwich Albion), Lucy-Jayne Grant (Galway United).

Midfielders: Chloe McCarron and Aimee Kerr (both Glentoran), Joely Andrews (Hibernian), Brenna McPartlan (Burnley), Connie Scofield (Sheffield United), Emily Cassap (Sunderland).

Forwards: Lauren Wade and Keri Halliday (both Hearts), Simone Magill (Birmingham City), Casey Howe (Celtic), Kerry Beattie (Portsmouth), Cora Chambers (Linfield), Kess Elmore (Sparta Prague).

articles.title: Former Real Madrid legend Gareth Bale partners with $1bn American investment firm exploring €500 million takeover of one of Spain's biggest and oldest clubs in bidding war against Saudi investors
articles.summary: Gareth Bale is set to advise an American investment group in their pursuit of acquiring Sevilla FC, seeking to transform the club's fortunes after years of decline.
articles.body: Gareth Bale could be preparing for an unexpected return to Spanish football, although this time his ambitions extend beyond the pitch. The former Real Madrid and Tottenham forward is reportedly advising an American investment group interested in acquiring Sevilla, the seven-time Europa League winners who have endured several difficult seasons. With the club seeking fresh investment and multiple parties considering bids, Bale’s latest move could bring him closer to the football ownership ambitions he has discussed since retiring.Gareth Bale linked with investment group interested in buying SevillaAccording to Spanish publication El Confidencial, Juggernaut Capital Partners is among the investment groups exploring a potential takeover of Sevilla, with Bale reportedly involved in an advisory capacity. The Welshman is not understood to be leading the proposed acquisition personally, but his association with the American fund places him within a group considering an investment in one of Spanish football’s most recognisable clubs.The Washington DC-based private equity firm manages more than $1 billion in investor capital and was founded in 2009. Bale joined forces with the company and its managing partner, John Shulman, in June 2026, when they launched Juggernaut Diversified Sports, a dedicated platform focused on sports investment. The new sports fund has a target below $1 billion, distinguishing its intended fundraising from the larger pool of capital managed by Juggernaut Capital Partners.The firm already has experience in the sports industry, having backed KemperSports, a golf course management company, and Thrill Sports, a Las Vegas-based business involved in action sports and combat entertainment. Bale also has an existing investment in TGL, the technology-driven indoor golf league founded by Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy, giving him commercial interests beyond his former football career.Sevilla are available for acquisition as the club seeks investment following several seasons of financial losses. Investment bank Goldman Sachs is reportedly overseeing a process involving the potential sale of up to 85 per cent of the club’s shares, with a valuation of approximately €500 million, equivalent to around £417 million. Bidders have reportedly been given until mid-December 2026 to submit proposals, with a takeover potentially completed in early 2027.Why Sevilla need investment after years of sporting declineSevilla's appeal to potential investors is difficult to separate from the contrast between their European achievements and recent domestic struggles. The Andalusian club have won the Europa League seven times, more than any other side, establishing a reputation for performing particularly well in the competition despite frequently operating outside Spain's traditional title contenders.Their recent league performances, however, have been considerably less convincing. Sevilla have failed to finish in the top half of La Liga in each of the previous four seasons, while their 2024-25 campaign brought them dangerously close to relegation. They finished that season just one point above the relegation zone, a position far removed from the club's standing during its most successful European campaigns.The situation has not improved sufficiently during the current campaign, with Sevilla sitting 13th in La Liga ahead of their forthcoming Seville derby against Real Betis. Their need for fresh capital extends beyond improving the first-team squad, particularly given the financial losses that have prompted the current sale process.The club's European history nevertheless gives potential investors an established identity and considerable commercial recognition. Sevilla have built a particularly strong relationship with the Europa League, winning the competition seven times and developing a record that remains unmatched by any other club. Their challenge is restoring the consistency required to compete more regularly near the top of Spanish football, rather than relying on their European reputation alone.Bale's Cardiff City takeover attempt and his ambitions beyond footballThe reported Sevilla interest follows Bale's unsuccessful attempts to acquire his boyhood club, Cardiff City, during 2025. Two formal takeover bids were launched, but the club's owner, Vincent Tan, ultimately declined to sell, preventing the former Wales captain from completing a return to the team he supported growing up.Bale subsequently made clear that the failed Cardiff discussions had not ended his interest in football ownership. Speaking to Front Office Sports in June 2026, after the launch of Juggernaut Diversified Sports, he explained that finding the appropriate investment opportunity remained more important than rushing into an acquisition.“It's about being patient, finding the right club, and the right path for us to take. That doesn't mean Cardiff is off the table. But I think now we have a bit of time and will look around.”His involvement with Juggernaut provides a potential route into ownership through an established investment operation, rather than requiring him to finance an acquisition independently. Bale has an estimated personal fortune of approximately £120 million, accumulated through his playing career, endorsements and investments, although his reported role in the Sevilla discussions remains advisory.During his career, Bale scored 226 goals in 664 appearances for club and country before announcing his retirement in January 2023, aged 33. He spent the final three years of his playing career in Major League Soccer with Los Angeles FC, having previously represented Tottenham, Real Madrid and Southampton. His career also included five Champions League titles with Real Madrid and a central role in Wales reaching the semi-finals of Euro 2016.Who else is competing to acquire Sevilla?Juggernaut Capital Partners are not the only potential investors examining the opportunity, with two other groups reportedly interested in acquiring shares in Sevilla. One is HD Ventures, an investment group led by Saudi brothers Mansour Sayed and Haidar Sayed, who are understood to be pursuing a rival proposal.The other is a local Seville consortium led by Antonio Lappi and Federico Quintero, whose involvement would offer a potential alternative to the international investment groups. The presence of several interested parties could complicate negotiations, particularly with the club's valuation and the proposed shareholding structure still central to any agreement.Sevilla have also been linked with another former Real Madrid player, Sergio Ramos, who previously pursued a controlling investment in the club alongside a consortium. However, that proposed transaction fell through in late May 2026, with reports suggesting disagreements emerged after the terms of the deal changed during negotiations.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "Nuestro compromiso es que el fútbol femenino esté presente siempre, no sólo cuando se gana"
articles.standfirst: Reyes Bellver, directora de fútbol femenino en la RFEF, abrió la segunda edición del Congreso Eleva
articles.summary: Reyes Bellver, directora de fútbol femenino en la RFEF, abrió la segunda edición del Congreso Eleva
articles.body: El Congreso Eleva se ha convertido en un punto de encuentro del ecosistema del mal llamado fútbol femenino. La segunda edición, que se celebra este jueves y viernes en la Ciudad del Fútbol de Las Rozas, cuenta con un panel con profesionales de la talla de Sarai Bareman, directora de fútbol femenino de la FIFA; Miraildes Maciel 'Formiga', una de las grandes leyendas internacionales; Emma Sykes, directora de desarrollo del fútbol femenino de la UEFA; Laura McAllister, vicepresidenta de la UEFA; Thanh Ha, secretaria general adjunta de la Federación de Fútbol de Vietnam; Meskerem Tadesse, responsable de desarrollo del fútbol femenino de la CAF; Katrien Jans, responsable de fútbol femenino de la Federación Belga de Fútbol; o Laura Georges, directora de desarrollo estratégico del fútbol de la FIFA. Después de la apertura del Congreso llevada a cabo por Álvaro de Miguel, secretario general de la RFEF, tomó la palabra Reyes Bellver, directora del fútbol femenino del ente, que expuso ante los presentes el plan de acción que se está llevando a cabo y que cimentó sobre cinco pilares: excelencia, liderazgo, especialización, visibilidad y acción. "Excelencia es no conformarse nunca, sostener el máximo nivel competitivo cuando ya has alcanzado la cima; es ganar hoy pero estar preparando ya a quienes ganarán mañana", apuntó. "El fútbol femenino también tiene que dirigirse, entrenarse y arbitrarse", recalcó. "Especialización no es copiar un modelo, es construir el nuestro, nuestra identidad. Se trata de un modelo propio, sostenible y excelente", subrayó. "Tenemos el compromiso de que el fútbol femenino esté presente siempre, no sólo cuando se gana; ser visibles es la condición para crecer", aseguró. "El plan cuenta con más de 70 objetivos concretos y más de 300 indicadores que hacen que el fútbol femenino se mueva del plan a la acción y de la acción al resultado", sentenció.

articles.title: La Fundación Real Madrid abre en Bod una escuela de fútbol para 40 niños
articles.standfirst: El proyecto, financiado por la Țiriac International Foundation, combina los entrenamientos con apoyo escolar, orientación a las familias y formación para los profesores
articles.summary: El proyecto, financiado por la Țiriac International Foundation, combina los entrenamientos con apoyo escolar, orientación a las familias y formación para los profesores
articles.body: Cuarenta niños en situación de vulnerabilidad social participarán en la nueva escuela sociodeportiva que la Fundación Real Madrid ha inaugurado en Bod, en la región rumana de Brașov. El fútbol será la base de un programa que busca favorecer la inclusión social y trabajar valores con la metodología de la fundación madridista. La escuela forma parte de Stronger Together: Education and Sport for Inclusion, un proyecto que la Fundación Real Madrid desarrolla junto a FDP Protagoniști în Educație. Lo financia la Țiriac International Foundation, una de las principales entidades filantrópicas de Rumanía, y cuenta con la colaboración de Olympus România, la Escuela Gimnazial de Bod y el Ayuntamiento de la localidad. Al acto de inauguración acudieron representantes de la Țiriac International Foundation, Olympus România y el Ayuntamiento, además de la dirección del centro escolar y los profesionales que desarrollan el programa. Allí se presentó el plan de trabajo, que suma a las sesiones de fútbol apoyo educativo, orientación a las familias y formación del profesorado en educación inclusiva. En esas tareas participarán los centros escolares, las autoridades locales y la comunidad educativa. "En la Fundación Real Madrid creemos que el deporte es mucho más que un juego, es una poderosa herramienta para la educación, la inclusión y el desarrollo personal", señaló Elena Fernández, jefa de Proyectos Europeos de la Fundación Real Madrid. Andra Farcaș, responsable de Acción Social de la Țiriac International Foundation, explicó el motivo de su apoyo: "Al apoyar este programa queremos contribuir a crear oportunidades reales para aquellos niños que necesitan ayuda para continuar su educación y mirar hacia su futuro con confianza". Visita a las escuelas de Bucarest La delegación de la Fundación Real Madrid aprovechó el viaje a Rumanía para visitar las escuelas sociodeportivas de los sectores 3 y 6 de Bucarest, que también desarrolla junto a FDP Protagoniști în Educație. Durante las visitas, los representantes de la fundación observaron los entrenamientos, entrevistaron a las familias y organizaron actividades participativas con los niños y el personal del proyecto. El objetivo era conocer de primera mano cómo valoran las sesiones, revisar su funcionamiento y evaluar su impacto en los participantes.

articles.title: Oficial: Tchouaméni renueva con el Madrid hasta 2032
articles.standfirst: El Real Madrid anuncia la ampliación del contrato del futbolista francés
articles.summary: El Real Madrid anuncia la ampliación del contrato del futbolista francés
articles.body: El Real Madrid y Aurélien Tchouameni han acordado la ampliación del contrato del centrocampista francés, que queda vinculado al club hasta el 30 de junio de 2032. El centrocampista francés amplía así su vinculación con el club blanco por seis temporadas más y refuerza su continuidad en el proyecto madridista, donde se ha consolidado como una pieza importante en el centro del campo. Con esta renovación, el Real Madrid lanza un mensaje claro sobre la importancia de Tchouaméni en su proyecto deportivo. El club apuesta por la continuidad de uno de los futbolistas llamados a marcar el presente y el futuro de su centro del campo y blinda su posición con un contrato de larga duración, hasta 2032. Una muestra de la confianza que existe en el internacional francés, que afronta su quinta temporada en el Santiago Bernabéu y que, a sus 26 años, todavía tiene un amplio recorrido por delante con la camiseta blanca. El Madrid se asegura así a un jugador que ha ido ganando peso dentro de la plantilla y que está llamado a seguir siendo una pieza importante en los próximos años. La renovación de Tchouaméni se suma a los movimientos que el Real Madrid está llevando a cabo para asegurar la continuidad de su núcleo joven. Apenas 24 horas antes, el club anunció la ampliación del contrato de Arda Güler hasta 2032, mientras que Jude Bellingham también tiene garantizada su vinculación con la entidad madridista hasta 2031. Tres operaciones que reflejan la apuesta del Real Madrid por consolidar una base de futbolistas con presente y mucho recorrido por delante. El club quiere mantener la continuidad de un centro del campo que está llamado a marcar una época en el Bernabéu y ha empezado a blindar a sus principales protagonistas con contratos de larga duración. Aurélien Tchouameni llegó al Real Madrid en 2022. En sus cinco temporadas defendiendo nuestra camiseta, ha disputado 205 partidos y ha ganado 8 títulos: 1 Champions League, 2 Mundiales de Clubes, 2 Supercopas de Europa, 1 Liga, 1 Copa del Rey y 1 Supercopa de España. Es internacional con Francia, selección con la que ha jugado 50 partidos hasta el momento y ha ganado 1 Liga de Naciones en 2021.
