The Georgia Bulldogs have one final Top 25 test to pass in the regular season in Week 12.

Kirby Smart's top-ranked team heads on the road to face the South Carolina Gamecocks for its final game of SEC regular-season play.

A victory basically guarantees UGA's spot in the 12-team College Football Playoff field no matter what happens in the rivalry game with the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets, or in the SEC Championship Game.

The SEC's other marquee matchup of Week 12 pits the LSU Tigers against the Tennessee Volunteers.

LSU is slight road favorite despite a slew of struggles in Lane Kiffin's first year as head coach.

Both SEC battles should have tremendous weather for mid-November.

All of the forecasts for Week 12's best games can be found here on The Weather Channel.

Prediction: Oregon 23, Michigan State 17

No. 11 Wake Forest (-20.5) at Georgia Tech

Prediction: Wake Forest 42, Georgia Tech 10

Forecast: Mostly Cloudy, Showers Likely, High of 60°F

Forecast: Mostly Cloudy, Chance of Showers, High of 76°F

Prediction: Houston 31, West Virginia 16

Forecast: Mostly Cloudy, Chance of Rain, High of 49°F

No. 1 Georgia (-15.5) at No. 21 South Carolina

Prediction: Georgia 37, South Carolina 13

Prediction: Louisville 38, Pittsburgh 17

San Diego State at No. 17 Boise State (-17.5)

Prediction: Boise State 41, San Diego State 21

Georgia's been a wrecking ball of a team in the last three weeks.

The top-ranked Bulldogs outscored three Top 25 opponents by a 117-36 margin. A similar fate should await them at Williams Brice Stadium on Saturday night.

South Carolina is ranked 21st, but it is a flawed football team that just got walloped on the road by the Arkansas Razorbacks last week.

The Gamecocks are 2-2 against Top 25 teams this season with wins over Tennessee and the Florida Gators, but they also struggled in a 49-18 loss to the Alabama Crimson Tide.

Alabama is the closest of South Carolina's four ranked opponents to Georgia's quality, which is why it's hard to give the Gamecocks much of a chance, even for a primetime home game.

Georgia's defense is playing on another level right now and its offense is coming off back-to-back 40-point performances.

If the Gunner Stockton-led offense puts up similar numbers in great conditions on Saturday night, South Carolina most likely won't be able to keep up.

Tennessee is a surprising underdog at home against LSU.

There is some concern about the status of Tennessee quarterback George MacIntyre, but according to On3's Pete Nakos , he isn't expected to miss any time.

Regardless of who starts at quarterback, Tennessee still has one of the best defenses in the country.

The Vols held the Texas A&M Aggies and Kentucky Wildcats to single-digit point totals in the last two games.

On the other hand, LSU's had trouble slowing down the top offenses in the SEC.

Lane Kiffin's Tigers are also at the end of a brutal three-game stretch that featured losses to the Texas Longhorns and Alabama Crimson Tide.

LSU is a worn-down team with no CFB Playoff aspirations. It's hard to see the Tigers finding the right motivation to get up for a third tough game in a row against a relentless Vols defense.

articles.title: BS Meter on the Latest Transfer Rumors for November 2026
articles.summary: Three months into the season, clubs are beginning to settle on their transfer plans for January.
articles.body:
Three months into the season, clubs are beginning to settle on their transfer plans for January.

With some movement on the manager market recently, intrigue over the potential incomings and outgoings in the winter window is ramping up, and we're here to dissect the latest transfer talk with our BS meter.

As covered in this edition, the most prepared clubs are even gearing up for next summer already.

So, which rumors should have you already imagining how a player will fare at their next club? Read on to find out.

Manchester United Interested in Calvin Bassey

With new manager Mauricio Pochettino in place, transfer plans will be front of mind for a Manchester United team clearly lacking in a few areas.

One of those is at centre-back, where Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez have proved difficult to trust, and Matthijs de Ligt's injury issues remain a major question mark. Ayden Heaven and Leny Yoro, 20 and 21 years old, respectively, may have some promise, but a more experienced, reliable option will be needed.

So, it makes sense that Matt Law of The Telegraph reported United have been discussing options for January, with Fulham's Calvin Bassey "expected to feature prominently" in those talks.

Bassey, 26, has made 104 Premier League appearances for Fulham since joining from Ajax in 2023 and has proved to be a consistent performer over that time.

His left foot also adds to his potential value at Old Trafford, given United's struggles to find a reliable option at left-back. His athleticism could make him better suited than their current options to modern defensive systems that frequently leave defenders in one-on-one situations.

This signing wouldn't raise United's ceiling significantly, but Bassey is good enough to help them move away from relegation trouble before ideally becoming more of a rotation option in future years.

Verdict: Not BS, but Fulham may need to stand firm to keep themselves clear of relegation trouble.

Weston McKennie Also on Pochettino's Radar

Sticking with Pochettino's transfer plans, Gazzetta dello Sport has linked the new Manchester United manager with one of his former United States men's national team players: Juventus midfielder Weston McKennie.

United's urgent need to pick up points cannot be overstated. They currently sit in the league's relegation zone, and while Pochettino will be keen to build something lasting in Manchester, he must balance the desire to strengthen the team's foundations with immediately steering them clear of danger.

Adding players familiar with his methods could be something of a cheat code for that quick turnaround. McKennie started every game for Pochettino at the World Cup in the summer, so he would come in with an immediate familiarity with the Argentinian's methods and demands.

However, United brought in three new midfielders this summer—Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba—for a combined total of more than $190 million. Baleba's impact has been limited by injury, and Santos and Tielemans have so far struggled across 24 combined appearances.

But a big part of Pochettino's remit will be to improve the performances of current players, and United would be better served upgrading other areas before making further midfield signings.

Verdict: BS, and McKennie seems to agree .

Luka Vušković has played just 10 games in the Premier League since joining Brighton & Hove Albion in the summer, but he is already appearing on the radar of some of the world's biggest clubs.

According to Florian Plettenberg of Sky Germany , the centre-back is on Liverpool's shortlist for a summer move, with Brighton valuing him at over $100 million. If the Croatian wants to move on from the south coast, there will be a lengthy queue for his services, with Plettenberg noting Vušković wants to eventually play for Real Madrid.

It's a lofty ambition, but the 19-year-old's career has been on a consistent upward trajectory since making his debut for Hajduk Split as a 16-year-old, and his decision to swap the chaos of Tottenham Hotspur for the relative calm of Brighton in the summer suggests he and his representatives have clear ideas on how to continue his development.

Vušković's lack of top-end speed will likely be elite teams' biggest concern. According to FotMob , his top speed for this season sits at 30.6 kilometers per hour, among the lowest marks for Premier League centre-backs. For comparison, the 35-year-old Virgil van Dijk has hit a top speed of 34.9 kph this season.

While there are ways to cover for a slower centre-back tactically, it would likely require Liverpool to add athleticism around him, potentially at full-back and in midfield.

That said, though, Vušković is dominant in the air and beginning to look the part in possession too, and those attributes should be enough to make him an excellent addition if Liverpool are able to accommodate his lack of pace.

Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott is a wanted man.

Mark Douglas of The i Paper reported that Arsenal have joined Chelsea and Liverpool in exploring a move for the 23-year-old, whose contract runs until summer 2028. Bournemouth are reluctant to sell in January, however, and Scott is understood to be happy to stay until the summer.

Chelsea have looked an obvious destination for Scott since the summer window closed without them having replaced Enzo Fernandez after he departed for Manchester City, while Liverpool's failure to add a midfielder in the summer also raised eyebrows.

Arsenal, though, are a more surprising contender. The Gunners added Bruno Guimaraes to an already strong midfield in the summer, and Scott would have to compete with seven other fully fledged internationals for playing time if he joined Mikel Arteta's team.

Perhaps this interest is bad news for some of those players. Martín Zubimendi has played just 107 Premier League minutes this season, while Mikel Merino and Eberechi Eze have only made three league starts between them.

If Arsenal were able to move some of those players along, the 23-year-old Scott would be a fine addition, but that would still leave him competing with Martin Odegaard, Declan Rice, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Guimaraes for minutes.

For a player with hopes of representing England at the 2028 European Championships, playing time will surely be a key factor in Scott's next move, and Arsenal look to be a considerably less attractive option in that regard than other contenders.

Bayern Munich insider Christian Falk reported that the German champions remain interested in a move for Liverpool's Rio Ngumoha after exploring a deal in the summer.

Liverpool would likely be disappointed to lose the 18-year-old winger, who has begun to be integrated into the England senior team, but Falk reported Bayern were willing to pay around $77 million last summer for a player who has started just one Premier League game this season.

With his contract expiring in 2028, Liverpool could face a difficult decision if no new deal is agreed before next summer. Ngumoha might also have reason to consider his options, given Liverpool's investment in Bradley Barcola and the potential impact on his first-team opportunities.

And while Bayern are hardly short of attacking talent themselves, there does look to be a spot opening up on their left side. Winger Luis Diaz is approaching 30 years old and has been suggested as a potential target for teams in Saudi Arabia.

Even if the Colombian remains in Germany beyond next summer, Ngumoha could still feature more regularly for Bayern than he has for Liverpool so far this season.

The Merseyside club will be desperate to keep Ngumoha, but his contract offers him a good amount of leverage given the potential he's already shown, and a move therefore can't be ruled out.

Transfers between Manchester United and Manchester City are rare, but United have again been linked with a move for left-back Rayan Aït-Nouri.

Florian Plettenberg reported in early November that the 25-year-old remains on the Red Devils' radar. In September, Simon Stone of BBC Sport reported that United failed in a bid to sign Aït-Nouri on loan, but Plettenberg's report suggests a permanent deal may now be of interest.

The increased urgency can probably be explained by events following the summer window, with United sitting 18th in the Premier League and having rolled out a rather unsatisfactory rotation of Luke Shaw, Diogo Dalot, Patrick Dorgu, Ayden Heaven and Noussair Mazraoui at left-back this season.

Aït-Nouri also hasn't played a single minute in the Premier League, so it should be a deal that suits all parties. However, the emotions surrounding footballing rivalries can be powerful enough to outweigh logic, and United's ownership may not want to risk losing further fan support by doing business with their neighbors.

Their situation may be dire enough for supporters to worry less about where a player has come from, but it's also questionable whether a marauding wing-back is even what United need when they are already struggling defensively.

Quite simply, though, United need a warm body at left-back, and they could do a lot worse than one who recorded 11 Premier League goal contributions in his last season as a regular starter.

articles.title: Bowl Projections, 2026 Playoff Predictions, CFP Bracket Picture Heading into Week 12
articles.summary: Tuesday's rankings for the CFB committee didn't include many major surprises, though they didn't exactly provide clarity for the final playoff picture either.
articles.body:
Tuesday's rankings for the CFB committee didn't include many major surprises, though they didn't exactly provide clarity for the final playoff picture either.

Wake Forest would be in the tournament if the season ended today, while 12th-ranked Texas Tech would be out and replaced by the highest-ranked Group of Six team, which is currently Boise State. The two could potentially flip before the end of the year, and there's also a chance that a three-loss Big Ten team sneaks into the bracket.

Oregon and Ohio State both jumped in the rankings after losses by teams like Kentucky and Houston.

How might the final playoff push unfold? Let's take a look at what lies ahead and make a few predictions.

Wake Forest and Texas Tech Are the Race to Watch

There are a few interesting races to watch over the final weeks of the season, but the most pivotal will probably be between Wake Forest and Texas Tech.

Wake Forest is barreling toward a spot in the ACC Championship Game and can clinch this week with a win over Georgia Tech and some help. Miami, which is undefeated in conference play, is likely to hold one spot, while Louisville is also in the mix.

Texas Tech, meanwhile, is fighting for a spot in the Big-12 title game. The Red Raiders and second-ranked Utah are the only Big-12 teams that can clinch a spot in the conference championship this week.

If Texas Tech beats Baylor and BYU loses to Kansas, the Raider Raiders would be in.

The problem for Texas Tech is that it needs help. Wins over Baylor and Cincinnati might not be enough if Utah and BYU both win out. Wake Forest, meanwhile, can set itself up nicely with wins over Georgia Tech and Duke.

The Demon Deacons' only loss this season was in a 33-20 game against Miami. If Wake Forest faces the Hurricanes in the ACC title game and can keep it close, that could be enough to earn the final at-large bid. A blowout loss, however, could open the door for Texas Tech and other fringe contenders.

Fans of the Oregon Ducks and Ohio State Buckeyes aren't out of hope just yet. However, the top two three-loss Big-Ten teams will need help.

If there's one thing we've learned over the last couple of years, it's that the CFP committee will do what it wants. Still, it's hard to see Oregon or Ohio State getting in with three losses if Wake Forest and Texas Tech both win out through the regular season.

Oregon will finish against Michigan State and Washington, while the Buckeyes will finish against Nebraska and Michigan. There isn't a quality win to be found in that group, and neither team is likely to push into the Big-Ten title game.

UCLA and Indiana will be headed to the conference title game if they both win out.

Of course, we've seen plenty of upsets during the 2026 season, so the door isn't completely shut. If BYU falters and allows Texas Tech into the conference title game, lopsided losses by the Red Raiders and Demon Deacons could at least force the committee to consider putting another Big-Ten team into the tournament—likely Oregon, which owns the head-to-head tiebreaker over Ohio State.

While unlikely, Indiana could also open a path to the conference championship game by falling flat against Washington and Purdue.

In other words, Ducks and Buckeyes fans should be rooting for chaos over the final few weeks.

articles.title: Expert CFB Locks, Predictions for LSU vs. Tennessee and Week 12 Biggest Games
articles.summary: Pull up a schedule. Any schedule. Take a look at what is coming up.
articles.body:
Pull up a schedule. Any schedule. Take a look at what is coming up.

No, we're not worried about the College Football Playoff or peculiar conference championship game tiebreakers. Our focus is far simpler than that.

Now, there's no need to panic. We know the drill; we've been here before. All we can do now is enjoy every remaining minute and make the most of the games we have.

As we dive deep into Week 12, this mentality has never felt more real. With Thanksgiving around the corner, things are heating up. Our picks, after a few "meh" weeks, need to pick up, too.

We haven't bet many totals this year. We're changing that in this spot.

It's been a rollercoaster at LSU, and we're not just talking about the season. The narrative surrounding the coach and quarterback have escalated, and the vibes are not great after a crushing loss against Texas.

Once again, the Tigers had no shortage of opportunities to beat a team handily. Once again, turnovers and missed opportunities proved to be the difference.

In particular, Sam Leavitt's three interceptions doomed this team. His six red-zone interceptions this season have likely cost LSU a shot at the playoff.

As for Tennessee, the team is winning ugly. That's not a bad thing. Right now, given the lack of star power at quarterback, it's actually a wonderful thing.

The offensive line is solid, the running game is unrelenting and, best of all, they have largely found a way to win regardless of the opposition.

As for this game, it just feels ugly. Tennessee wants to hang onto the ball, LSU might not have maximum motivation and the end result could be a sloppy, tight football game.

If you have bet against UCLA this season, you have not done well.

In fact, until last weekend, you had lost each and every bet you've made. We've been on the wrong side a few times this season; we've also been on the right side.

Through it all, the Bruins have stayed unbeaten.

Ty Dieffenbach has played a significant role in making this possible. Once the backup QB, Dieffenbach was named the starter when Nico Iamaleava was lost for the season due to injury.

Last week, Dieffenbach left his team's game against Illinois with what appeared to be a shoulder issue. He was also walking with a limp. Despite the issues, Dieffenbach returned and helped guide his team to another win.

Michigan was throttled by Oregon 31-7, totaling just 286 yards. Both Tommy Carr and Bryce Underwood played, but neither played well. It was the latest ugly performance for the Wolverines in a season of ugly performances.

Despite that showing, look at this point spread.

With a total in the 30s, this feels like a low-scoring, ugly football game, regardless of who Michigan starts at QB.

We're not proud of this, but we're sticking with it.

College football is a game of speed and ability. It is also, and this is why we love it, a game of emotion.

This brings us to Utah, one of the few unbeaten teams remaining. The Utes are coming off a thrilling, late-night win at Arizona that featured seven lead changes. The Wildcats ultimately covered, although the Utes left with the unbeaten season intact.

Which brings us to this week and one of the larger hangover spots on the football calendar.

Not only did Utah play a thriller on Saturday. The week prior, Utah beat rival BYU at home in a matchup that featured plenty of dramatics.

Meanwhile, TCU is nowhere near a perfect football team. In fact, the Horned Frogs are 5-5.

Interestingly enough, all five of TCU's losses have come by one score or less. The Horned Frogs also nearly beat Arizona on the road a few weeks ago. In fact, they should have won.

With the total hovering in the mid-40s, defenses could be a theme. While TCU doesn't do anything exceptionally well, they're solid in all phases.

Playing against a team on a multi-week rollercoaster that will hit the road for the second consecutive week, you'll want to keep an eye on this one. Upset brewing.

On the topic of highly rated Big 12 teams facing a precarious spot, enter BYU.

One team is 8-2; the other is 4-6. While we recognize how different these two teams are, the oddsmakers think the difference between them, at least in this setting, isn't that unique.

The Cougars will hit the road for the last time this season, playing an early football game against an opponent that has been a mixed bag this year. On the topic of road games, BYU lost its previous trips to Utah and Central Florida. It also didn't play particularly well at TCU, winning a close game by a touchdown.

For Kansas, what version are we getting? Maybe more specifically, which Isaiah Marshall are we getting?

The KU quarterback has sensational athleticism. He's coming off back-to-back games with at least 125 yards rushing. As long as he doesn't turn the ball over, which is a big if at times, he can really produce.

On the road for four of its last six games, the Jayhawks should find comfort in playing at home. The defense played well last week, limiting West Virginia to just 262 yards of offense.

It will struggle to duplicate that effort against a solid BYU offense, although it should be able to keep up offensively.

At the risk of repeating ourselves, we'll say it once more. Don't be shocked if we see an upset here.

Are you sensing a theme? We promise this isn't by design.

More than anything, our picks this week highlight the Big 12's sheer absurdity and volatility. While the conference's best teams have largely avoided carnage, that could very well change.

As for the opponent, Baylor has certainly had plenty of highs and lows.

When Dave Aranda was fired, Joe Klanderman was named interim coach. Until last week, when his team lost by three touchdowns to BYU, things were progressing nicely.

Quarterback DJ Lagway has played significantly better football. He should be able to test a Texas Tech defense that isn't the same unit we saw a season ago.

Still, the Red Raiders were excellent last week against Oklahoma State. Quarterback Thomas Castellanos was particularly sharp. His arrival has been nothing short of season-saving.

Despite that performance, Baylor feels very much alive. Another week on the road against another quarterback with loads of physical talent could present a much different outcome than the one we just saw.

Want to see carnage in the Big 12? We're not asking for it, but we might see it.

Last week wasn't fun for either team, although Kentucky has scored just 20 points over its last two games. Missouri has struggled lately, though playing two of the nation's best teams hasn't helped. It'll look much better this week.

While East Carolina has won three consecutive games, they were against Temple, USF, and Charlotte. Army has lost two in a row, although one of those losses came against Memphis. This feels like a get-right moment.

Navy's No. 3-ranked rushing attack is facing off against Memphis' No. 126-ranked rushing defense. That could spell trouble. It's been a rough year for Navy as a whole, but this could change that narrative.

articles.title: Top Heisman 2026 Contenders to Watch in Race for College Football's Biggest Honor
articles.summary: As the college football world winds through what's left of the 2026 season, the Heisman Trophy race remains too close to call.
articles.body:
As the college football world winds through what's left of the 2026 season, the Heisman Trophy race remains too close to call.

And that says plenty about the strength of these candidates given the kind of campaign Ohio State's star receiver Jeremiah Smith is delivering.

Smith has, in the eyes of oddsmakers at least, established himself as the favorite, but he isn't without major competition. Miami quarterback Darian Mensah is applying the most pressure, but Utah quarterback Devon Dampier is forcing his way into the conversation, too.

It should be a thrill ride from here, so let's do some table-setting with odds and arguments for the top Heisman contenders.

Jeremiah Smith, WR, Ohio State -140 (bet $140 to win $100)

Darian Mensah, QB, Miami +370 (bet $100 to win $370)

The Utes own both a 10-0 record and the No. 2 spot on our latest expert rankings . Dampier's fingerprints—and footprints—are all over this success.

The all-purpose producer has completed 66.5 percent of his passes for 2,257 yards and 22 touchdowns (against eight interceptions). He has ran for another 582 yards and nine scores, and he even has a 29-yard reception on his resume.

He might have the most helium of any player in this race. He also might have the most ground to cover since he doesn't have the star power or name recognition of Smith or Mensah.

All Dampier can do is keep the pedal floored and hope his numbers speak the loudest by season's end. If he pilots this team to a 13-0 season and a Big 12 title, voters may struggle to find great arguments against him.

Mensah is about as efficient as it gets at the quarterback position. He leads the FBS with a 76.3 completion percentage, and he has tallied 29 touchdowns against just two interceptions.

He has legitimate "Wow!" numbers from just about every angle. What he hasn't had for the past two weeks, though—and may not for the rest of the regular season—is star receiver Malachi Toney, who had tightrope surgery following a high ankle sprain earlier this month.

Mensah was awesome this last weekend without him (30-of-41 for 328 yards and a touchdown), but he was less than awesome the week prior. While he still managed to pass for 269 yards and three touchdowns, he threw an interception and completed a season-low 55.8 percent of his attempts. Miami also suffered its lone loss of the campaign (31-24 to Notre Dame).

Still, the Hurricanes hold a clear path to the ACC Championship, meaning Mensah has a chance to make plenty more noise. If he remains this efficient while becoming a 12-win conference champ, he could wind up with the richest resume in the field.

The loss of junior quarterback Julian Sayin to a fractured elbow did irreperable damage to the Buckeyes, who've suffered two double-digit losses during the three games he's missed. It somehow hasn't, however, caused Smith to miss any kind of step.

Despite adjusting on the fly to a true freshman quarterback (Luke Fahey), Smith has continued stockpiling monster stat lines. During Fahey's three starts, Smith has totaled 28 receptions for 333 yards and three touchdowns.

Smith's numbers on the season—which obviously isn't even over yet—could make even elite gamers envious. He's already sitting on 80 receptions for 1,317 yards and 15 touchdowns. He has scored in all but one game (a 56-point rout of Kent State), and he has four multi-score efforts.

There is little question he is the most electric talent in college football. The only question is whether Ohio State's late-season, Sayin-less slide could sway voters toward someone else.

articles.title: Peterborough United chairman Darragh MacAnthony 'fighting for his legacy'
articles.summary: Darragh MacAnthony says he is "working around the clock" to protect his "legacy" as Peterborough United chairman.
articles.body:
Darragh MacAnthony says he is "working around the clock" to protect his "legacy" as Peterborough United chairman, with the club facing another fight to retain their League One status.

Posh's hierarchy had targeted promotion in 2026-27, but are 22nd in the third-tier, having finished 18th in the past two seasons.

Peterborough sacked manager Luke Williams after 11 months in charge in September and appointed Robbie Savage, but they are on a run of no win in seven games in all competitions.

Last month, MacAnthony "promised" to sell his 75% stake in the club after 20 years as chairman if they had not reached League One's top 10 by February.

On Tuesday, MacAnthony issued a lengthy statement on the club's website , external in which he said he "would not outstay my welcome at this amazing club".

"If we don't turn things around, I will look to put the club in the hands of someone who can do a better job than me, because that is the right thing to do," the statement added.

"It is not something I want to do or need to do, but if it is right for our club, it will get done. You have my word on that."

MacAnthony sold half his stake to Jason Neale and Stewart Thompson in 2018, through their Canadian business Kelgary Sports and Entertainment, but became sole majority shareholder again five years later after they stood down from the board.

"I am working around the clock to make sure my legacy as owner will not be defined by this season," MacAnthony said.

"I have been in this game long enough to know there will be more downs before the highs return, but I have staked my ownership on the highs returning.

"I have done that because, as always, I am an eternal optimist, and I honestly believe our club, our players and our staff will turn this awful time around for you, our fans."

articles.title: Manchester City charges: Premier League clubs to cover legal costs if sponsors sue
articles.summary: Premier League clubs vote to provide legal cover to the organisation's five board directors in the event Manchester City's sponsors sue them.
articles.body:
Premier League clubs have voted to cover legal expenses for the organisation's five board directors if any of Manchester City 's sponsors sue them.

The clubs met in London on Thursday for the first time since City were found guilty of a catalogue of charges relating to the breaching of financial rules by an independent commission in September.

City have appealed and maintain their innocence, with a sanction yet to be decided.

The club's sponsors Etihad and Etisalat have both said they are considering legal action against the Premier League.

At present, under the league's articles of association, a director is only financially covered should they win a legal case brought against them by a third party. But the league's rules will now be updated to extend legal indemnity for CEO Richard Masters, chair Alison Brittan and three other non-executive directors .

City and Nottingham Forest were the only two clubs that voted against the proposal to provide extra legal protection, with the other 18 clubs voting in favour.

Due to collective responsibility, it means that all clubs are now liable to cover legal costs that could run into hundreds of millions of pounds, raising the intriguing possibility of City being financially impacted by the legal action of its own sponsors.

It is understood City's CFO Ingo Bank asked Premier League chair Brittan during Thursday's meeting if the proposal was a direct result of threats of legal action from Etihad and Etisalat, but she said she could not comment.

While Forest have declined to comment, their objection to the proposal is said have to been on procedural grounds, rather than due to any support for City.

The club did not believe that sufficient information had been provided, or adequate time afforded, for clubs to properly consider the implications of the proposed amendment, particularly given the potentially significant financial responsibilities involved. It felt that such a decision warranted more scrutiny and informed consideration before clubs were asked to vote.

An independent commission appointed by the Premier League found City guilty of artificially inflating the club's revenues by over £830m over a nine-year period in September.

The commission determined that the club arranged "sham" contracts with sponsors, which disguised funding from club owners the Abu Dhabi United Group.

Premier League CEO Masters said City "systematically broke Premier League rules for nearly a decade".

In October, City sponsor Etihad Airways said it was considering legal action against the Premier League .

In a statement, the United Arab Emirates-based airline said it "categorically rejects any finding, conclusion or implication that suggests the airline has ever been involved in improper commercial arrangements".

Etisalat signalled its intention to follow suit earlier this month and described the Premier League's verdict as "entirely false and defamatory".

articles.standfirst: Los ocho miembros europeos del Consejo de la FIFA, entre ellos Ceferin, reclaman explicaciones y acceso a la documentación solicitada sobre distintos asuntos
articles.summary: Los ocho miembros europeos del Consejo de la FIFA, entre ellos Ceferin, reclaman explicaciones y acceso a la documentación solicitada sobre distintos asuntos
articles.body: Los representantes europeos en el Consejo de la FIFA han elevado el tono de sus reclamaciones al organismo que preside Gianni Infantino. En una carta fechada el 16 de noviembre y dirigida a la Secretaría General, los ocho miembros denuncian que siguen sin recibir respuesta a las preguntas que trasladaron los días 19 y 23 de octubre, ni tampoco la documentación que solicitaron entonces. "Hasta la fecha, la FIFA no ha respondido a ninguna de esas preguntas. Tampoco ha facilitado ninguno de los documentos solicitados ni ha indicado cuándo tiene previsto hacerlo", señalan en el escrito. Una reclamación que vuelve a poner el foco en la falta de transparencia del organismo, especialmente en torno al proyecto FIFA Entreprise (FFE), la fallida propuesta para comercializar los derechos del Mundial. Los firmantes, entre los que se encuentra Aleksander Ceferin, presidente de la UEFA y vicepresidente de la FIFA, cuestionan también la oferta de la organización para permitirles revisar parte de la documentación. Según denuncian, el acceso estaría limitado a determinados "documentos clave" relacionados con el proyecto FFE, todavía sin especificar, y sujeto a unos "estrictos protocolos de revisión" sobre los que tampoco han recibido información. Los ocho representantes recuerdan que su condición de miembros del Consejo les otorga derechos y responsabilidades tanto bajo la normativa de la FIFA como conforme al derecho suizo. Por ello, consideran que necesitan acceder a los documentos y materiales pertinentes para cumplir adecuadamente con sus obligaciones. Antes de organizar un desplazamiento a Zúrich para examinar la documentación, exigen que la FIFA detalle qué archivos estarán disponibles, si podrán consultar toda la información relativa a los asuntos planteados y cuáles serán las condiciones de acceso. También reclaman una explicación sobre los motivos por los que el organismo pretende imponer esas limitaciones. "Somos plenamente conscientes de nuestros deberes fiduciarios hacia la FIFA y de nuestra obligación de actuar en el mejor interés de la organización y de sus miembros. Precisamente por eso hemos planteado nuestras preguntas y solicitado no solo respuestas, sino también acceso a la documentación pertinente", sostienen. La carta concluye con un mensaje directo a la cúpula del organismo. "En última instancia, se trata de saber si el presidente y la administración de la FIFA reconocen su responsabilidad ante el Consejo", advierten. Además, dejan claro que cualquier revisión de documentos no supondrá una renuncia a sus derechos para reclamar esa información en procedimientos judiciales actuales o futuros en Estados Unidos. Como último gesto, los ocho firmantes han enviado una copia de la carta a todos los integrantes del Consejo de la FIFA.

articles.title: Football tragedy: 18-year-old Argentine player Abel Núñez dies after being struck in head by ball during youth match
articles.summary: The sports community mourns the tragic death of 18-year-old Argentine football player Abel Núñez, who died from a head injury sustained during a youth match, prompting tributes from FC Ezeiza and Deportivo Muniz.
articles.body: Argentine football is mourning the death of Abel Nunez, an 18-year-old youth player who died two days after suffering a devastating head injury during a match for FC Ezeiza. Nunez collapsed after being struck by a fiercely cleared ball from a Deportivo Muniz defender, leaving medical staff rushing to treat him before he was taken to hospital for emergency surgery. The match was abandoned, and tributes have since poured in from both clubs following his death.How Abel Nunez suffered fatal head injury during youth football matchNunez was playing for FC Ezeiza against Deportivo Muniz in a Juveniles C fixture, part of Argentina's youth football league system, on Friday when the incident occurred. The teenager was struck in the head by a ball cleared by a Muniz defender who was under pressure, with the force of the impact causing him to collapse on the pitch.Local sports journalist Cristian Rompani, who regularly covers youth football, witnessed the incident and described the moment, as quoted by The Sun. He said the match had been relatively calm, despite being scrappy, before the defender made the clearance.“A Muniz defender under pressure cleared the ball. It was his only option,” Rompani said. “He struck it with unusual power. In my nearly 30 years in youth football, I’ve never seen a kick like that.”The ball travelled at a low height and struck Nunez from just four or five metres away. Rompani described the impact as resembling a boxing knockout, saying the teenager fell immediately and appeared completely unresponsive.“The ball didn’t gain any height, and just four or five metres away, it struck Abel in the head,” he recalled. “It was like a knockout. The boy collapsed, completely unresponsive.”Medical staff attended to Nunez on the pitch, with the match subsequently suspended. Rompani said the doctor examined the teenager without moving him and later told him that Nunez's breathing had appeared unusual. The 18-year-old was taken to hospital, where doctors found a fractured skull and internal bleeding. He underwent emergency surgery but died on Sunday, two days after the incident.FC Ezeiza and Deportivo Muniz pay tribute after teenager's deathBefore Nunez's death was confirmed, FC Ezeiza had appealed to its community to support the young footballer as he underwent treatment. The club published an emotional message asking players, families, coaches, officials and supporters to come together and hope for his recovery.“At FC Ezeiza, we want to send all our strength, affection, and support to Abel Nunez, who is going through a very difficult time after suffering a severe blow to the head that required surgery,” the club wrote.“Today, we want to come together as a family, setting aside any differences, to join in wishing for his speedy recovery and hoping that everything turns out well. We invite the entire club community, families, players, coaching staff, management and friends to join this chain of prayers, sending him all the positive energy and strength he needs to pull through.”Following confirmation of his death, FC Ezeiza shared a photograph of Nunez wearing the club's No. 10 shirt, alongside a message announcing the loss of a young player who had been part of its football community.“The hardest news we have ever had to share as a club,” the statement began. “With profound pain and immense sadness, we say goodbye to a young man who had his whole life ahead of him, a loss that leaves an indescribable void.”The club said Nunez had been proudly representing Ezeiza when he suffered the injury, adding that football had become secondary to the loss of a team-mate and a young man with dreams and ambitions.“Today, football fades into the background. We are overcome with the pain of saying goodbye to a team-mate, a young man full of dreams and aspirations, who was a cherished part of our family.”FC Ezeiza also extended its condolences to Nunez's family, friends and team-mates, and pledged its support during what it described as an incredibly difficult time. Deportivo Muniz, the club involved in the match, also issued a statement expressing its condolences.“With deep pain and immense sadness, we wish to send our most sincere condolences to Abel’s family, to his friends, and to the entire FC Ezeiza institution. There are no words for this moment,” the statement read.Who was Abel Nunez, the Argentine teenager who died aged 18?Nunez was born in 2008 and came from Ezeiza, a city on the outskirts of Buenos Aires in Argentina. He played both football and futsal regularly, according to details shared on his Facebook profile, and was part of FC Ezeiza's youth set-up.Nunez's death comes amid another recent tragedy in professional football. Less than a fortnight earlier, 30-year-old Jesus de Miguel, a striker for Spanish second-tier club Tenerife, died in hospital following a collision with an opposing goalkeeper during a match.The goalkeeper involved, FC Andorra's Jesus Owono, was sent off and subsequently received a 12-match suspension. He also remains the subject of a police investigation.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: FIFA Under-17 World Cup 2026 gets under way in Qatar despite USA withdrawal
articles.summary: The 25-day tournament will feature 48 teams, with Dominican Republic replacing USA as FIFA plays down security concerns.
articles.body:
The FIFA Under-17 World Cup has kicked off in Qatar, with 48 teams participating in the global youth football competition despite the United States’ withdrawal over security concerns last week.

The tournament, which opened with two concurrent matches on Thursday, will be played in the 2022 World Cup host nation over the next 24 days after FIFA dismissed security concerns in the country.

“Everyone is safe in Doha,” FIFA President Gianni Infantino said in the Qatari capital last week.

US Soccer withdrew its national team citing safety concerns last Thursday, but the sport’s global governing body, which is hosting the tournament, said at the time that its plans remained unchanged.

Qatar has not been targeted by missiles since July as a result of the US-Israel war on Iran.

“The safety and security of all participants and fans remain paramount. As with all FIFA tournaments and events, we are in close contact with the relevant authorities and ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌are looking forward to the tournament kickoff in Qatar,” FIFA told Al Jazeera in a statement hours after the USA’s announcement.

“In recent months, Qatar has successfully hosted several international events,” it added.

Qatar hosted two major international tournaments in the past two weeks.

MotoGP’s Qatar Grand Prix was successfully held on November 8 and the FIP Padel World Cup 2026 ended on the same day.

The tournament will be hosted at the competition complex in Aspire Zone, Qatar’s central sporting hub.

The December 13 final will be played at the Ahmad 8 hours ago (12:33 GMT) bin Ali Stadium, which was a FIFA World Cup 2022 venue.

articles.title: Balde no se regala
articles.standfirst: El Barça quiere sacar tajada si se marcha el lateral
articles.summary: El Barça quiere sacar tajada si se marcha el lateral
articles.body: El futuro de Alejandro Balde es una incógnita. A nadie se le escapa que está viviendo una situación muy complicada porque ha perdido mucho protagonismo en el Barcelona, donde se ha visto superado en su demarcación por Cancelo y Xavi Espart. No es algo nuevo, ya que en los últimos seis meses de la pasada campaña vivió una situación similar, con el portugués jugando mucho más que él. En verano, Balde no quiso irse, pero ahora la situación ha cambiado. El Barcelona, que vería con muy buenos ojos una salida porque, además, ayudaría a financiar la llegada de un central, juega al despiste. «Es de la casa, es un jugador importante. Hay etapas en las que juegas más o menos. Balde está preparado para cuando el míster lo necesite. ¿Venderlo en invierno? No», dijo Bojan cuando se le preguntó por la situación del lateral. Lo que no va a hacer el Barcelona es regalar a su futbolista. Y eso es lo que haría si públicamente confirmara que quiere venderlo. El asunto lo está llevando Jorge Mendes, agente del futbolista, que sondea por Europa en busca de un destino para su representado. Hay varios clubes interesados, pero, de momento, no hay ninguna oferta formal. Su salida no se activará hasta que haya un posible destino y Balde comunique al club que desea marcharse. «Las alineaciones se hacen por dinámicas. Balde ha hecho temporadas muy buenas y ha demostrado su nivel. Si me dices que nunca hemos visto a un Balde a gran nivel... Pero no es así. Después está la parte del jugador, pero no nos ha dicho nada de que no esté contento; no es el caso», añadió Deco. Es decir, deja claro que, aunque en este momento no sea así, Balde ha demostrado en otros años que es un excelente jugador. Su precio de mercado está en torno a los 40 millones. El Barça quiere vender y quiere hacerlo bien. Por eso, la opción de una cesión no gusta en Can Barça. De momento, se abre un compás de espera hasta que Mendes llegue con una oferta acorde con la calidad del lateral. No hay que olvidar que estamos a mes y medio de que se abra el mercado.

articles.title: Kompany revive su hospitalización: "Quizás no le hice suficiente caso a mi cuerpo"
articles.standfirst: "Tampoco puedo restarle importancia, ¡fue todo un shock!", ha asegurado el técnico del Bayern de Múnich, que este viernes volverá a sentarse en el banquillo, ya recuperado de una meningitis
articles.summary: "Tampoco puedo restarle importancia, ¡fue todo un shock!", ha asegurado el técnico del Bayern de Múnich, que este viernes volverá a sentarse en el banquillo, ya recuperado de una meningitis
articles.body: Kompany se sentará de nuevo en el banquillo del Bayern de Múnich este viernes en el encuentro ante el Colonia de la Bundesliga. El técnico, ya recuperado de una meningitis por la que ha tenido que estar hospitalizado, ha vuelto esta semana a dirigir los entrenamientos del equipo alemán tras haber estado fuera cinco partidos. En su comparecencia ante los medios, el míster ha recordado el momento en el que se desplomó en una sesión de trabajo del Bayern. "Simplemente estaba enfermo, como probablemente le pasó a todo el mundo en octubre y noviembre. Quizás no le hice suficiente caso a mi cuerpo. Y todo lo que vino después fue simplemente una consecuencia de eso, nada grave, nada especial. Pero tampoco puedo restarle importancia, ¡fue todo un shock!", ha dicho. Kompany se desmayó el 23 de octubre durante un entrenamiento y tuvo que ser trasladado de urgencia a un hospital, donde le trataron una meningitis. Una vez que recibió el alta, continuó su recuperación en casa y su segundo, Aaron Danks, asumió la dirección del equipo. “Todas las pruebas que me hicieron después dieron muy buenos resultados. Así que, la verdad, estoy muy sano. Afortunadamente no fue tan grave como para tener consecuencias mayores”, explicó. “En este momento de calma, uno siempre intenta aprender algo. También me pareció interesante observar al equipo desde una perspectiva diferente: a mi cuerpo técnico, a mis compañeros, cómo trabajan, qué hacen, cómo resuelven esta situación. Fue un momento realmente fascinante. Me siento muy bien y estoy feliz de estar de vuelta con el equipo”, terminó Kompany.

articles.title: España cerrará el año con probaturas
articles.standfirst: Sonia Bermúdez da este viernes la convocatoria para los amistosos ante Chile y Venezuela
articles.summary: Sonia Bermúdez da este viernes la convocatoria para los amistosos ante Chile y Venezuela
articles.body: Sonia Bermúdez dará este viernes la lista de convocadas para los amistosos que España disputará ante Chile y Venezuela los próximos 28 de noviembre y 4 de diciembre en León y A Coruña respectivamente. Una relación de jugadoras en las que se esperan grandes ausencias y muchas novedades a fin de dosificar esfuerzos y probar a futbolistas que hasta a fecha no han tenido su oportunidad. Resulta prácticamente imposible aventurarse a especular con la nómina de futbolistas que completarán la convocatoria de la selección española en esta ocasión. Una ventana internacional en la que España ha tenido problemas para encontrar rivales, ya que muchas de las grandes potencias están aún disputándose la clasificación para el Mundial de Brasil -véase Inglaterra, Italia, Países Bajos, Noruega o Portugal entre otros- o bien ya tenían cerrados previamente amistosos para estas fechas o bien han declinado la opción de enfrentarse a la número 1 del ranking FIFA, y que ha solventado con dos rivales inéditos en el historial de nuestra selección. Chile, número 49 del ranking FIFA, será el rival de España el sábado 28 de noviembre (18:00 horas) en el Reino de León. La selección dirigida por Luis Mena viene de quedar séptima (de nueve selecciones) en la Liga de las naciones y por ende quedarse sin opciones de clasificación para la cita mundialista del próximo verano. Por su parte, Venezuela, 42 de la clasificación mundial, se enfrentará a España el viernes 4 de diciembre (21:00 horas) en el estadio de Riazor en A Coruña. El equipo dirigido por Ricardo Belli, que ya anunció su nómina de convocadas, quedó tercera en la Liga de Naciones (sólo por detrás de Colombia y Argentina) y disputará en febrero -junto a Ecuador, Papúa Nueva Guinea, Uzbekistán, Taiwán, Ghana, Sudáfrica y otras tres selecciones aún no definidas- el torneo interconferencias que otorgará las últimas tres plazas para Brasil 2027. El carácter amistoso de los duelos y el nivel de los rivales hace prever que Sonia pueda probar a jugadoras menos habituales o con las que no ha contado hasta la fecha. La madrileña, que ya ha hecho debutar a nueve futbolistas bajo su batuta -véase Clara Serrajordi, Edna Imade, Martina Fernández, Ornella Vignola, Aiara Agirrezabala, Clara Pinedo, Andrea Medina, Natalia Ramos y Ainhoa Marín- podría aumentar esta cifra en los próximos compromisos internacionales.

articles.title: Undefeated HSFB HC Resigns After Team Was DQ'd From Playoffs Over 53-Second Roster Error
articles.summary: A high school football coach in New York resigned after his team was disqualified from the state playoffs due to fielding an ineligible player.
articles.body:
A high school football coach in New York resigned after his team was disqualified from the state playoffs due to fielding an ineligible player.

Middletown High School coach Tim Strenfel stepped down Tuesday, according to Blaise Gomez of News 12 Hudson Valley. Mid-Hudson News' Justin Rodriguez reported the disqualification "was not the sole factor in his decision," as he had already been weighing his future on the sideline.

Middletown defeated Valley Central High School 48-15 in the Section IX Class AA semifinal. However, the result was voided because Middletown fielded a kicker who wasn't eligible to compete in the playoffs. The player in question only had 53 seconds of game time and didn't score any points.

Assistant coach Isaac Cayetano told Gomez that Strenfel got the green light from the school's athletic director to add the player, who was on Middletown's soccer team to the football roster. However, Strenfel didn't know the kicker had failed to satisfy the minimum requirement (three games) in order to suit up in the postseason.

"You can blame him. You can blame me. You can blame everyone on the staff," Cayetano said. "However, we have bosses as well, and we have people who are supposed to educate us."

Valley Central went on to defeat Newburgh Free Academy 16-6 in the final and advanced to the regional championship.

articles.title: Turno para Le Normand
articles.standfirst: El central español tendrá que llenar las ausencias de Pubill y el Cuti Romero
articles.summary: El central español tendrá que llenar las ausencias de Pubill y el Cuti Romero
articles.body: No está viviendo su mejor momento como rojiblanco. Robin Le Normand tendrá que volver a escena el domingo frente al Getafe tras vivir ante el Bayern uno de sus días más bajos con el Atlético. El internacional español se retiró del campo en el minuto 59 después de que los de Simeone encajaran el primer gol ante los germanos. El central colchonero recorrió el terreno de juego junto a sus compañeros para agradecer el apoyo de la afición, totalmente abatido. Fue una de sus noches más duras desde que llegó al Atlético. Y es que ahora, con las bajas del Cuti Romero y Marc Pubill, todo apunta a que el ex de la Real Sociedad regresará a la titularidad para compartir el centro de la zaga con David Hancko. Simeone no tiene muchas más alternativas para perfilar su pareja de centrales. Con el eslovaco entrenando ya como uno más tras regresar de su periplo internacional, Le Normand se perfila como su acompañante. El internacional español ha ido perdiendo peso esta temporada hasta convertirse en el cuarto central en cuanto a minutos disputados. Con 464 minutos sobre el césped, Robin aparece, como decíamos, como el cuarto central rojiblanco. Hancko es indiscutible para Simeone, mientras que Pubill acumula minutos tanto de central como de lateral. El Cuti Romero, por su parte, se ha convertido en una pieza angular de la defensa y solo las lesiones le han apartado del once. Por eso, el peso de Le Normand ha ido disminuyendo en lo que va de temporada. Ante el Getafe tendrá una importante prueba de fuego para intentar recuperar su mejor versión. El campeón de la Eurocopa con España suma 11 partidos esta temporada. Tan solo ha sido titular en cinco de ellos, siendo el último el disputado ante el Bayern en el Metropolitano. Un encuentro que acabó con derrota rojiblanca y con el central señalado en la jugada del primer tanto. Unas semanas después tiene la oportunidad de sacarse la espina del duelo ante los alemanes. Con las lesiones de Pubill y del Cuti Romero, Simeone necesita encontrar en Le Normand la misma fiabilidad que ofrecían sus compañeros ausentes.

articles.title: Mario Frick: Aberdeen's new head coach targets Scottish Premiership top-six  with 'heavy metal football'
articles.summary: The 52-year-old has replaced Stephen Robinson at Pittodrie; the Dons are 11th in the Scottish Premiership; his first game in charge is at Kilmarnock on Saturday; watch Rangers vs Aberdeen on November 24, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The 52-year-old takes over with the side sitting 11th in the table following Stephen Robinson's dismissal after their 4-0 defeat at Hibernian before the international break.

Frick, who played 125 times for Liechtenstein, previously took charge of the national youth teams in his homeland before spells with Vaduz and Luzern, helping the latter to avoid relegation.

"I had a very long career as a professional, so I know the pressure and I'm always optimist," he said.

Asked why he was confident of success, he added: "[Luzern] they were on the bottom of the table with 18 matches and 11 points and the whole environment was sad and we saved them.

"I'm pretty sure we can do this also in this place and I'm very ambitious.

"It's very important to get out of this situation but we want to go in the top six."

Frick will take charge for the first time on Saturday at bottom side Kilmarnock and he is determined to make an immediate impact with his style of football.

"Heavy metal," he said. "That's high pressing, that's counter-pressing vertical play creating many goalscoring chances."

Aberdeen have scored just 12 goals in the league this season while conceding 18 and Frick, who spent most of his playing career as a centre-forward, wants better.

"I'm known for high-scoring clubs. With Vaduz we had the goal record," the former St Gallen player said.

"Everything is lacking to score and so I'm here to change that.

"We have to improve now. We need time but we don't have, so it's more important to show the basics.

"Body language, willing to work, intensity. That's what I want to see."

The Aberdeen supporters booed Robinson off the pitch at the end of what was ultimately his final game at Pittodrie.

With just two home league wins this season, the morale of the Red Army is at a low.

Chief executive Adrian Bevington revealed Frick was the "unanimous decision," although his appointment took most by surprise.

"I'm not here to win with the fans, I'm here to win with my team.

"The supporters are amazing here I know that and but I'm not here to win them. The most important thing is the team and not me."

Frick faces an immediate relegation battle, starting with a run of five fixtures in just 15 days.

His first match is a trip to bottom of the table Kilmarnock. A win would move them five points clear, a defeat would see the Dons drop to 12th.

Next is a tough test against Rangers and former Aberdeen boss Derek McInnes at Ibrox, live on Sky Sports. The Dons have failed to win any of their last eight games against the Gers, losing to them in the Premiership and League Cup already this season.

There is no doubt Frick has taken charge of a team low on confidence, with four straight defeats ultimately leading to his predecessor's dismissal.

He has said he is "very hungry and ready to level up players" and, after playing most of his career as a centre-forward, he wants his team "playing forward and trying to score".

Time is not on the new manager's side. Robinson took four games before his first win, but with the prospect of ending the weekend bottom of the table, Frick will be aiming for a faster start to his Dons career.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino: Man Utd boss priorities include Fernandes, culture and defence
articles.summary: Culture, defence and Bruno Fernandes - the key issues facing Mauricio Pochettino as he takes over as Manchester United boss.
articles.body:
"We have to find a way to create the best habits and culture that makes us close to winning every single game."

Mauricio Pochettino has used his first interview as Manchester United head coach to outline his vision for the club.

The former Tottenham, Paris St-Germain and Chelsea boss wasted no time getting across the Atlantic Ocean after completing his stint in charge of the United States on Tuesday.

He met key staff on Wednesday, took training for the first time on Thursday and conducts his first wider media conference at United's Carrington training ground on Friday.

The 54-year-old is facing a packed schedule, starting with a trip to Anfield to face Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday.

Pochettino accepted a big challenge. United are 18th in the table. By 17:00 GMT on Saturday, they could be bottom.

So, what are the Argentine's priorities as he begins the task of trying to transform United's season?

"To create the culture is the most important [thing]," he told United's in-house media in a 15-minute introductory chat.

Pochettino's first Man Utd training session filmed by drone operator

Manchester won't always be blue - Pochettino

Fitness obsessed & 'control freak' - what can Man Utd expect from Pochettino?

'Making the players feel like winners again'

It would be easy to point to areas of the pitch where United have been deficient this season. However, it cannot be totally dismissed that virtually the same group of players were transformed over the second half of last season by the recently sacked Michael Carrick, who guided them to third in the Premier League and Champions League qualification.

Remarkably, Pochettino has won twice as many matches in charge of the USA this season than the three victories United have managed, with a 100% record from six games.

United, by contrast, have not won in the Premier League since August, while two of their three victories have required the Red Devils to come from behind. Their single clean sheet came against Azerbaijan outfit Sabah FK in the Champions League in September.

One of the most immediate tasks for Pochettino will be to alter the mindset of players who seem to have become restricted by the pressure they have found themselves subjected to.

"It is a mistake to see the situation," he said. "We need to see the potential of this club.

"We need to understand it is a game, and to connect with the game we need to feel free. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is our priority now; to work with them and take the pressure.

"Pressure needs to bring energy. Responsibility needs to bring energy because if not, it is too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back."

That said, there are some glaring issues that Carrick was unable to fix and Pochettino must find an answer to. The most obvious is defence.

Who should the cornerstones of United's defence be?

The Carrick regime felt Leny Yoro was the player with the attributes - pace, strength and control - most suited to their needs. Yet, at 21, Yoro is prone to mistakes and he has also been needed at right-back because regular right-backs Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui have, at times, been required on the left.

Lisandro Martinez and Matthijs de Ligt have not been reliable fitness wise. Pochettino knows the baggage attached to Martinez, given his post-match criticisms of the club hierarchy after the 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid, and the knowledge his fellow countryman's contract expires in the summer.

Harry Maguire has started all 10 league games this season but suffered a back spasm in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, immediately before the international break, and had to be replaced at half-time. Maguire has many attributes, but his presence does restrict the ability to press high up the field.

Ayden Heaven has made eight appearances in all competitions but has previously been regarded as being behind Yoro in terms of his overall development.

The 27-year-old was consoled by Joshua Zirkzee when he was replaced against Villa, such was the negative fan reaction to his performance, which included conceding a penalty at the start of the second-half.

It can justifiably be argued if Dalot has the talent to match the 260 club appearances he has now made.

However, for his faults, coaches love his attitude.

Dalot has been described to BBC Sport as having one of the most committed and professional approaches to the game, that he is someone willing to take responsibility, happy to play in unfamiliar positions if it benefits the team, the first to offer support to team-mates, and a positive influence in the dressing room.

Bruno Fernandes' alarming drop off in form has been one of the most noticeable features of the current campaign.

The Portugal playmaker has been a shadow of the star who scooped all the player of the year awards last season and broke the Premier League assist record.

He was axed for the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth after criticising Carrick's tactics in the 4-1 Champions League humiliation by Como and seems to be affected by concerns around his future - his contract also expires in the summer, although United are almost certain to trigger their one-year option on the 32-year-old - and the summer arrival of Youri Tielemans.

For the short term at least, Pochettino must decide whether to pick Fernandes in his favoured number 10 role and work around that, or drop him deeper, as Ruben Amorim did, or play him wide, which has not brought the best out of him.

Fernandes' status affects other areas. Carrick never seemed convinced by Andrey Santos, a £50m summer arrival from Chelsea. But with £70m Carlos Baleba out for an extended period, a partner needs to be found in midfield for Kobbie Mainoo.

Tielemans did not seem to have the running ability for the role, and Amorim wouldn't pick Mainoo with Fernandes.

Further forward, with Benjamin Sesko out, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo have tended to be used in the number nine role. But Cunha likes to drop deep, while, after a bright start to the season, Mbeumo has scored twice in his past 12 appearances.

Neither Shea Lacey nor Harry Amass have started a Premier League game this season. Both caught the eye on England Under-20 duty during the international break. Pochettino has history for giving young players a chance and the pair could benefit from that.

There is one issue Pochettino mentioned in his interview he will soon discover requires delicate handling.

United's match-going fans have stood by every manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired. There is no reason to think that will change now.

However, their relationship with the club's ownership is fractured, possibly beyond repair. Fresh accounts to 30 September show the club's overall debt remains more than £1.1bn and a further £14.5m was spent on finance costs in the previous quarter.

This fuels discontent in the stands, already heightened because of various ticketing measures, none of which are viewed by most supporters as being positive.

"We need to be united," said Pochettino.

"Chemistry is really important, chemistry between us and the staff and the fans and the players, the directors, the owners and everything."

articles.title: Premier League clubs vote to cover legal costs if Man City sponsors sue competition's board members
articles.summary: Premier League clubs met in central London this morning and voted by 18-2 to provide their board members with indemnity if they are sued individually in any potential defamation suits in light of the independent commission's finding the club entered into 'sham' contracts with sponsors
articles.body:
City are appealing after the commission found they had entered into "sham" contracts with sponsors.

Two of City's sponsors, Etihad Airways and Etisalat, have threatened the Premier League with legal action.

Premier League clubs met in central London this morning and voted by 18-2 to provide their board members with indemnity if they are sued individually in any potential defamation suits.

City and Nottingham Forest are believed to have voted against. A two-thirds majority - 14 clubs - was required to make the change.

The board members are chair Alison Brittain, chief executive Richard Masters, and non-executive directors Mai Fyfield, Dharmash Mistry and Matthew Ryder.

Abu Dhabi airline Etihad Airways have sponsored City since 2009. In a statement dated 30 September they said the Premier League did not engage with them and they were not given the chance to provide relevant information.

Etihad said it was seeking legal advice to protect their interests. Etihad were not named in the 40-page published decision but they said it had "created damaging implications" for them.

Meanwhile, Abu Dhabi communications company Etisalat says it is are also considering taking legal action against the Premier League.

In a statement, the company said: "Emirates Telecommunications Group Company PJSC (Etisalat) views the published findings of the English Premier League, as they relate to Etisalat, as entirely false and defamatory. Etisalat is actively considering all options relating to its rights and associated legal remedies in this matter."

Forest say PL vote was not in support of Man City

Sources close to Evangelos Marinakis and the Nottingham Forest board have said their decision to vote alongside Manchester City is in no way meant to show solidarity with a club that has been found guilty of serious financial breaches.

Forest and City were the only clubs who voted against the proposal to share any future legal costs which could be brought by some of City's sponsors who are threatening to sue the Premier League. The vote at the Premier League shareholders meeting was passed 18 votes to two.

Whilst Forest have declined to comment, sources have told Sky Sports News their objection to the proposal is procedural, rather than because of any support for City.

The East Midlands club felt that insufficient information had been provided, and that there wasn't enough time to consider the implications.

Forest felt that such a decision warranted more scrutiny and informed consideration before the matter was put to a vote.

What did the independent commission find?

Manchester City arranged "sham" contracts with a number of its commercial partners as part of a "disguised funding scheme" to artificially inflate the club's revenues by £830m.

The club filed accounts that concealed the true state of its finances.

Manchester City were significantly in breach of both the Premier League's and UEFA's spending limits and broke "well over 100" Premier League regulations.

Manchester City failed to co-operate and act in good faith towards the league during the investigation, with three out of four alleged breaches upheld and one charge not proven.

The commission also said it was "regrettable" that a decision had taken so long to reach, with the hearing having taken place between September and December 2024.

A Manchester City statement read: "Manchester City is both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League commission that has been published today.

"The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions relating to this case. The club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.

"The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements uncompleted. Manchester City will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.

"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.

"The club is obviously restricted in what it can say further until all future proceedings are complete."

Manchester City's statement erroneously refers to a Premier League commission. It is an independent commission .

articles.title: De la Fuente y Louzán ofrecen el título mundial al Apóstol en la Catedral de Santiago
articles.standfirst: "Fue un éxito de todo un país, de toda una nación", ha dicho el seleccionador
articles.summary: "Fue un éxito de todo un país, de toda una nación", ha dicho el seleccionador
articles.body: El seleccionador español de fútbol, Luis de la Fuente, y el presidente de la Federación Española de Fútbol, Rafael Louzán, ofrecieron este jueves el título mundial conquistado el pasado verano al Apostol en la Catedral de Santiago de Compostela, en una jornada muy intensa en Galicia en la que también fueron recibidos por el presidente de la Xunta de Galicia, Alfonso Rueda. El título fue "un éxito de todo un país, de toda una nación", dijo De La Fuente antes de reiterar su ambición porque "todavía hay muchas cosas por hacer", durante la recepción con Rueda en el salón noble del Pazo de Raxoi antes de acudir a la Catedral, donde no se permitió el acceso de la prensa. El titular del ejecutivo gallego desveló que la víspera de la salida de la selección desde Santiago hacia Estados Unidos había trasladado a Louzán su deseo de que la Copa visitase Galicia si España se proclamaba campeona. "La noche anterior a que salieran hacia Estados Unidos, le comenté a Rafa -Louzán- que cuando ganáramos el Mundial había que traer la Copa a Galicia en la víspera del Xacobeo de Santiago. Y ahora están aquí cumpliendo el compromiso de aquel día del presidente de la Federación", señaló Rueda. Cuatro meses después de que España derrotara a Argentina en la final del Mundial, Louzán y Luis de la Fuente, con la segunda Copa del Mundo que conquistó el equipo nacional, llegaron este jueves a la capital de Galicia. "Este acto es muy simbólico y este salón se reserva para momentos muy especiales, y este lo fue. En una nación tan variada como la nuestra, que todos tenemos nuestras identidades, muy potentes y variadas, no es fácil encontrar algo que nos una y la selección es algo que nos unió y nos hizo vibrar", comentó el presidente de la Xunta durante el acto celebrado en el salón noble del Pazo de Raxoi. El seleccionador Luis de la Fuente dijo que el título fue "un éxito de todo un país, de toda una nación", antes de reiterar su ambición porque "todavía hay muchas cosas por hacer". "Lo mejor está por llegar", declaró el técnico del equipo nacional, quien coincidió con el presidente de la Federación Española en agradecer el apoyo que han recibido de todos los españoles. "Venimos aquí a ofrecerle este título al Apóstol Santiago", afirmó Louzán, quien avanzó que por la tarde tendrán un acto, en el que participará el delantero del Celta y campeón mundialista Borja Iglesias, con la presencia de "más de 7.000 niños". El deán de la Catedral, Manuel Jesús Formoso, recibió a los portadores de la Copa del Mundo en la Praza do Obradoiro, donde turistas y vecinos desafiaron a la lluvia para pedir una foto al seleccionador antes de acceder a la Catedral. "Estoy muy emocionado, por presentarle al patrón de España este trofeo que ha sido ganado por todo un país y luego porque tengo muchos recuerdos de mi infancia en esta Catedral", comentó el entrenador español a los periodistas tras el acto de la ofrenda. Tras acordarse de su catolicismo, De la Fuente dijo que al Apóstol "solo" le ha pedido salud para seguir trabajando porque "con eso estamos todos felices", ya que a él le da igual el rival en el sorteo de la Liga de las Naciones porque "lo más importante es poder luchar por algo, pero también hay que disfrutar del camino porque nos quedan cosas maravillosas por disfrutar".

articles.title: Ian Evatt: Struggling Blackpool sack head coach on his 45th birthday
articles.summary: Blackpool sack head coach Ian Evatt after a year in charge following a run of one win and six defeats in their past 10 league games.
articles.body:
Blackpool have sacked head coach Ian Evatt on his 45th birthday after a year in charge following a run of one win and six defeats in their past 10 league games.

Evatt's final match was Saturday's 1-0 away defeat by fellow strugglers AFC Wimbledon , leaving the Tangerines immediately above the League One relegation zone.

That defeat, however, came after the he said his squad had been decimated by a sickness bug during their trip to the capital.

Evatt departs the Seasiders with the announcement made a matter of hours after the club wished him a happy birthday , external on social media.

In a statement, the club thanked Evatt for his efforts and said Steve Thompson will take charge for Saturday's game against Wigan Athletic.

Blackpool appointed Evatt, who won promotion from League One and the Championship during seven years as a centre-back for the club, as Steve Bruce's successor in October 2025.

During a six-year playing career at Bloomfield Road, Evatt made more than 250 appearances for the Seasiders.

On arrival as a manager, a tally of 13 points from a possible 15 in December 2025 lifted them out of the relegation zone, although they lost 10 and won two of their next 15 matches in all competitions.

They finished the campaign strongly, with six wins in seven games as part of a sequence of one defeat in 13 between mid-March and the end of August, only to struggle again as this season continued.

Speaking after their defeat by Mansfield in October, Evatt said he had "a huge amount of confidence" in his ability because of his record.

Evatt guided Barrow to the 2019-20 National League title in his first managerial role, then won promotion to League One with Bolton Wanderers the following season.

Wanderers went on to lift the 2022-23 EFL Trophy and reached the third-tier play-offs in consecutive seasons under Evatt, losing in the final in his final full campaign in 2023-24.

'It's been horrific' - Evatt says sickness bug decimated Blackpool

Evatt will retain legendary status despite exit - analysis

BBC Radio Lancashire sport editor Andy Bayes

After an encouraging start to the season, Blackpool's form has been alarming since the beginning of September, and owner-chairman Simon Sadler has decided a change was needed with 33 league matches still to play.

There have been mitigating circumstances but everyone in the hot seat is judged on their points return.

His final game in charge will undoubtedly go down as one of those factors. Illness within the squad made the defeat at Wimbledon somewhat understandable, but the performance should have warranted more.

Throughout Evatt's tenure, he was forced to constantly juggle an injury list that never seemed to ease.

The centre-back position was a recurring problem and is unlikely to be solved overnight. Steve Bruce signings Fraser Horsfall and Michael Ihiekwe have yet to make a league appearance this season, despite being expected to play a significant role after injuries at the back end of the last campaign.

Supporters wanted greater tactical flexibility and a system that would allow mercurial talents such as Josh Bowler to have a greater impact.

However, Evatt largely stuck with a wing-back formation, believing he did not have the personnel to play effectively in other ways.

He made an immediate impact after taking charge, but that was followed by a significant downturn in form before a recovery that secured League One survival last season.

This term, there had been hope that those struggles were behind Blackpool.

Evatt will retain legendary status for his achievements as a player, having won two promotions and played in the Premier League.

However, Blackpool are now searching for their eighth permanent manager or head coach since Sadler took over the club in the summer of 2019.

articles.title: Kevin Blackwell: Crawley Town name ex-Leeds United boss as manager until end of season
articles.summary: Crawley Town appoint Kevin Blackwell as manager until the end of the season after the 67-year-old's spell in temporary charge.
articles.body:
The EFL's bottom side Crawley Town have appointed caretaker boss Kevin Blackwell as their manager until the end of the season.

The 67-year-old took interim charge after Colin Kazim-Richards was sacked on 21 October with the club bottom of League Two and six points adrift of safety.

The Red Devils are unbeaten in the two league games Blackwell has overseen, drawing 1-1 with Tranmere Rovers before winning 1-0 away at Oldham .

They remain at the foot of the table and six points behind 22nd-placed Rochdale, although Crawley do have three games in hand on the Dale.

Crawley were dumped out of the FA Cup by seventh-tier Wimborne Town when they lost 2-0 in the first round earlier this month.

But the club said Blackwell has "made a strong impression on club leadership, making him a strong candidate for the role as the weeks progressed" since the departure of Kazim-Richards.

"The club has been working hard to make the right appointment and has been carefully weighing up the options to ensure the appointment is the right one for the team and the club as a whole," Crawley said in a statement on their website. , external

"Kevin's leadership skills, work ethic and desire have made a strong impression on club staff and the first-team squad, and the club's leadership team are committed to ensuring the positive mentality remains in the building as we approach a run of crucial games.

"Kevin has the full support of everyone at the football club, as we look to turn over a new page on our season and climb back up the table.

"In the coming weeks, Kevin will be making further appointments to his coaching team, following the recent arrival of Jordan Tait."

Blackwell has previously managed Leeds United, Luton Town and Sheffield United but this is his first permanent managerial role since leaving Bury in 2013.

Crawley host Fleetwood Town in League Two on Saturday afternoon (15:00 GMT) in Blackwell's first game in charge since landing the job on a permanent basis.
