articles.title: Louzán confirma que la FIFA no admite la candidatura conjunta del País Vasco para el Mundial
articles.standfirst: "Dice que hay dos sedes, así que ahora le toca a ellos decidir", ha dicho el presidente de la RFEF
articles.summary: "Dice que hay dos sedes, así que ahora le toca a ellos decidir", ha dicho el presidente de la RFEF
articles.body: El presidente de la Federación Española de Fútbol (RFEF), Rafael Louzán, confirmó este jueves que la FIFA no admite la propuesta de una sede única compartida entre Bilbao y San Sebastián para el Mundial 2030 de fútbol. "Se pedía que hubiera una sola sede con dos estadios y FIFA, en este momento, dice que no, que en el País Vasco hay dos sedes, así que ahora le toca a ellos decidir", declaró a los periodistas el presidente de la RFEF tras realizar una ofrenda con la Copa del Mundo al Apóstol Santiago en la Catedral de la capital de Galicia. En este sentido, Louzán avanzó que la idea del Gobierno vasco es que haya una sede conjunta "con dos estadios" -Anoeta y San Mamés-, algo que la FIFA no acepta. "Ahora le toca al Gobierno vasco y al alcalde de San Sebastián decidir qué papel quieren tener aquí", apuntó el presidente de la Federación, quien dijo que "sin duda" la final del Mundial 2030 será en España, aunque no quiso pronunciarse si será en Madrid o en Barcelona. El dirigente de la RFEF también reveló que "en las próximas semanas" emisarios de la FIFA acudirán a Vigo y Valencia para evaluar las candidaturas de ambas ciudades. "El resto va todo bien. La cuenta atrás ha empezado, ahora toca consolidar ese gran proyecto que tenemos de país para que sea un Mundial memorable para nuestro país", apuntó Louzán, quien mostró su deseo de que Balaídos acoja partidos de la próxima cita mundialista. "Vigo ahora tiene una oportunidad y ojalá pueda aprovecharla para ser una de las sedes. Mi compromiso es que Vigo pueda ser una de las sedes, pero eso no depende tanto de nosotros, depende más de la candidatura de ciudad y de que FIFA nos diga si reúne las condiciones", concluyó.

articles.title: El City empieza a sufrir bloqueos: pierde 2.000 millones en un día
articles.standfirst: El grupo inversor teme las sanciones que puedan venir para el club inglés
articles.summary: El grupo inversor teme las sanciones que puedan venir para el club inglés
articles.body: La multinacional Apollo ha cancelado un préstamo de unos 2.000 millones de dólares (unos 1.820 de euros) )al propietario del Manchester City tras el incumplimiento de normas por parte del club inglés y la posible sanción que se viene por parte de la Premier League, según fuentes del diario inglés 'Finantial Times'. Apollo Global Management, grupo estadounidense de capital privado que también opera en el Atlético de Madrid, se encontraba en la fase final de la negociación del préstamo a City Football Group. Sin embargo, la operación fracasó tras el dictamen emitido en septiembre por la comisión independiente de la Premier, que acusó a la institución de Mánchester de haber inflado artificialmente su situación financiera en más de 900 millones de libras a lo largo de nueve años. El club inglés fue declarado culpable de 114 cargos por incumplimiento de normas financieras, lo que plantea la posibilidad de una sanción importante que podría oscilar entre una multa y la deducción de puntos, hasta la expulsión de la Premier League. El club —propiedad, desde 2008, del jeque Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, miembro de la familia gobernante de Abu Dabi— ha negado haber cometido irregularidades y está apelando contra las conclusiones de que infringió las normas de gasto entre 2009 y 2018. El fracaso de las conversaciones con Apollo pone de relieve la incertidumbre que rodea al futuro financiero del Manchester City, a la espera del resultado de su apelación y del alcance de las posibles sanciones que se le impongan si se ratifica el dictamen de la comisión independiente.

articles.title: Rangers transfers: Derek McInnes on January window
articles.summary: Manager Derek McInnes says Rangers will only sell players in January if they receive offers that "makes the club blink".
articles.body:
Manager Derek McInnes says Rangers will only sell a player in the January transfer window if they receive an offer that "makes the club blink".

Players such as German striker Ryan Naderi, Mauritania winger Djeidi Gassama and Belgium midfielder Nico Raskin have been linked with moves while centre-back Olwethu Makhanya has attracted interest after an outstanding start to the season.

However McInnes will oppose moves for players who have featured regularly in his first season in charge at Ibrox - unless a club makes a startling offer that is too good to turn down.

"If somebody comes in way over the top then you have to obviously consider these sort of things," he said.

"But in the main, we're not looking to move players out, particularly players that have been playing regularly. We want to shut that down really early.

"We don't want agents flirting with clubs, giving them any encouragement. We know and understand that keeping that core of players and having that stability is so important for us.

"We don't want January window to be excitable or dramatic. Just to come and go and hopefully we can just keep doing what we're doing."

McInnes said that Lawrence Shankland and Cammy Devlin are progressing well in their rehabilitation and that his players returned unscathed from international duty - although Kevin Kelsy was back later than expected from the Venezuela squad.

"Kevin is the only wee anomaly. We didn't get him back from Russia on Wednesday night because of a few issues with transport, but we managed to get him back in at lunchtime on Thursday," McInnes said.

Rangers face Motherwell in Lanarkshire on Saturday and have a solid away record - but dropped points in two away draws prior to the win at St Mirren.

McInnes is expecting a stiff test as he believes the Steelmen are beginning to perform like the side that impressed throughout last season and qualified for Europe.

"I think they have got a lot of traits and similarities to the team that got a lot of success last year. I think over the last two or three games they've started to look a wee bit more like that," he added.

"They'll be a difficult opponent, but if we want to get to where we want to get to this season, we want to make sure we leave Motherwell with all three points."

articles.title: La paradoja de Sato: el Valencia busca equipo para el mejor jugador joven de Asia
articles.standfirst: El fichaje de verano se alza con el trofeo de la AFC por su rendimiento en Japón mientras el club tiene decidido cederlo en el mercado de invierno
articles.summary: El fichaje de verano se alza con el trofeo de la AFC por su rendimiento en Japón mientras el club tiene decidido cederlo en el mercado de invierno
articles.body: El futbolista japonés del Valencia Ryunosuke Sato fue elegido Mejor Jugador Joven de Asia 2026, en un acto organizado por la Confederación Asiática de Fútbol (AFC) en Bangkok, que confirma la progresión de una de las apuestas de futuro de la entidad blanquinegra. Sin embargo, el galardón llega en un momento en el que el Valencia trabaja precisamente para encontrarle una salida en forma de cesión durante el mercado de invierno. La dirección deportiva considera que el jugador necesita sumar minutos de competición y experiencia en el fútbol europeo, algo difícil de garantizar en la actual plantilla del Valencia, como ha demostrado el técnico Javier Aguirre desde que llegó al banquillo. El director deportivo, Braulio Vázquez, lleva semanas sondeando posibles destinos para el internacional japonés y trasladó este mismo asunto en la reunión mantenida el pasado martes con Corey Woolfolk, en Madrid. El principal ejecutivo deportivo de Pitchwise ya empieza a tomar posiciones a la espera de que el Consejo Superior de Deportes (CSD) autorice el desembarco accionarial en el club de Mestalla. Es total el consenso sobre la necesidad de buscar una cesión que acelere el desarrollo de un futbolista al que el club considera estratégico -deportiva o económicamente- a medio y largo plazo. La situación deportiva de Sato ha variado completamente desde que el Valencia confirmó su fichaje por 4 millones de euros en verano. De hecho, ha pasado de ser titular indiscutible con Carlos Corberán, a verse relegado al banquillo por Javier Aguirre y también en los dos partidos de Óscar Sánchez como interino. El técnico mexicano ya ha dejado claro en varias ocasiones que el japonés necesita tiempo de adaptación y continuidad para seguir creciendo, dos factores que ahora mismo resultan difíciles de encontrar en un Valencia asfixiado en la clasificación: "Le exijo que compita. Sin balón le pido más agresividad. La personalidad que muestra con la pelota, que la muestre sin la pelota", dijo el vasco de Sato, a pregunta de un periodista en una conferencia de prensa. El premio de la AFC reconoce una trayectoria ascendente y prometedora. Sato, que cumplió 20 años en octubre, fue elegido mejor jugador joven de la J1 League en 2025 tras su cesión al Fagiano Okayama y consolidó su explosión en 2026 con el FC Tokyo. Además, lideró a Japón en la conquista de la Copa Asiática sub-23, torneo en el que fue nombrado mejor jugador y terminó como máximo goleador con cuatro tantos. La AFC destacó también su irrupción con la selección absoluta japonesa y su llegada en LaLiga, donde se convirtió este verano en el primer futbolista japonés de la historia del primer equipo valencianista. Ahora, mientras recibe el mayor reconocimiento individual del fútbol asiático para jugadores jóvenes, el Valencia busca el destino adecuado para que esa promesa continúe creciendo lejos de Mestalla antes de regresar para competir por un puesto en el futuro.

articles.title: El Manchester United, en caída libre: aumenta sus pérdidas un 174 %
articles.standfirst: 18,1 millones en el primer trimestre fiscal de 2026, que incluye los tres meses previos al 30 de septiembre
articles.summary: 18,1 millones en el primer trimestre fiscal de 2027, que incluye los tres meses previos al 30 de septiembre
articles.body: El Manchester United aumentó las pérdidas después de impuestos un 174 %, hasta 18,1 millones, en el primer trimestre fiscal de 2026, que incluye los tres meses previos al 30 de septiembre En este período se incluye el periodo de fichajes veraniego, pero no el despido de Michael Carrick y el correspondiente finiquito de él y de su cuerpo técnico, y la contratación de Mauricio Pochettino, por el que el United tuvo que abonar una cláusula de rescisión de 10 millones de euros a la federación estadounidense. Uno de los aspectos más preocupantes de las cuentas del United es la deuda acumulada desde que la familia Glazer compró el club en 2005. El club tiene una deuda de 700 millones de euros, lo que supone un 19,2 % más que en el anterior periodo. Además, los sueldos se han incrementado un 8,6 % hasta los 70 millones de euros. Pese a este receso económico, el United sigue siendo uno de los clubes del mundo que más dinero genera y en dicho periodo sus ingresos crecieron un 4,1 % hasta 132 millones. La clasificación a la Liga de Campeones tras dos años de ausencia ha ayudado al aumento de los ingresos, ya que la recaudación en derechos televisivos ha subido un 17,7 % hasta 32 millones. El Manchester United comenzará este domingo una nueva era cuando Mauricio Pochettino dirija su primer partido como técnico frente al Liverpool en Anfield.

articles.summary: BBC Sport football expert Chris Sutton takes on world champion boxer Lauren Price, plus the BBC readers and AI, with his predictions for this weekend's Premier League fixtures.
articles.body:
Manchester United start life under new boss Mauricio Pochettino on Sunday but will they get their first Premier League win since August when they face Liverpool at Anfield?

"My worry for United is that they have one of the worst back fours in the Premier League," said BBC Sport football expert Chris Sutton.

"Their defensive record is something Pochettino will try to address but, whoever he picks, they are just not very good."

Sutton is making predictions for all 380 Premier League games this season, against AI, BBC Sport readers anad a variety of guests.

For week 11, he takes on boxer Lauren Price, who is an Arsenal fan.

She will defend her unified welterweight titles against Michaela Kotaskova on Friday, and has a shot at becoming Wales' first undisputed world champion after the vacant WBO welterweight title was added to the fight.

Price returns to home soil at the Utilita Arena in Cardiff for a fight that will be shown live on BBC Two and BBC iPlayer, from 21:00 GMT.

Do you agree with their predictions? You can pick your own below.

The most popular scoreline selected for each game is used in the scoreboards and tables at the bottom of this page.

A correct result (picking a win, draw or defeat) is worth 10 points. The exact score earns 40 points.

Want to make more predictions? You can play BBC Sport's new Match of the Day predictor game every week, featuring six fixtures from domestic and European competition.

Before turning to boxing, Price was a world kickboxing champion and international footballer - she captained the Wales Under-19 side, and played for the senior team as well as Cardiff City.

"My football days have helped me massively to get where I am in the ring today," the 32-year-old told BBC Sport.

"I honestly believe my footwork, and how fast my feet are, comes from when I played football.

"I am really proud of everything I achieved in football, especially playing for my country. It is the same now in boxing - to get in the ring and represent Wales is always an honour."

Price said the support of her grandparents helped her become successful at so many sports - and she followed her grandad, Derek, by becoming an Arsenal fan too.

"When I was a kid I was absolutely besotted with football and Arsenal were THE team when I was growing up," she explained.

"It was just the way they played under Arsene Wenger, and how they passed the ball - it was incredible. I loved Robin van Persie but Thierry Henry was my icon, my hero."

Chris Sutton and Lauren Price were speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

The wheels have come off for Enzo Maresca at Manchester City with three Premier League defeats in a row.

It's not just City's results which have been alarming, either - they were well beaten by Nottingham Forest last time out, and their performance would have been the biggest concern for their manager.

In contrast, Fulham 's results have improved of late and they are unbeaten in four league games. They've done all right whenever I've seen them this season, so I'm not surprised to see them picking up points.

Still, the international break probably came at a good time for Maresca to sort things out. Erling Haaland is scoring again too - not that he ever really stopped for very long - and I'm expecting City to be much better here.

I'm even going for them to keep a clean sheet, for the first time in eight games. I'm always brave... which is why I am bottom of the predictions table.

Lauren's prediction: City are having a tricky time of it at the moment but they should still win this. 2-0

I was at Sunderland 's win over Chelsea and they thoroughly deserved it. They had been on a dreadful run of results before then, but it was a reminder of what they are about.

Brian Brobbey was just phenomenal for the Black Cats in that game but, like his captain Granit Xhaka, he is injured and will miss out here.

That just makes me think Aston Villa will have the edge. I always fancy them at home anyway with the way they go after teams, although I don't think this will be easy for them.

Villa boss Unai Emery was fuming after his side threw away a two-goal lead twice in their 4-4 draw at Manchester United , but they will hold on this time while Sunderland go down fighting.

Lauren's prediction: Villa are going really well. 2-1

Bournemouth have won eight games in a row in all competitions and it is incredible how Marco Rose has turned things around after a slow start.

The Cherries were absolutely flying before the international break - but will the two weeks off affect their momentum?

Forest did not need the break either, after their brilliant win over Manchester City .

That was such an important result for their manager Oliver Glasner but I think they will find it difficult to follow it up at Bournemouth .

Lauren's prediction: Forest shocked City last time out but I am going with Bournemouth here, they are on a brilliant run. 2-1

Chelsea were so lethargic when I watched them lose against Sunderland , and I don't think they were hard done by in that game - they looked flimsy at the back, and were deservedly beaten.

I had a bit of a pile-on from some Chelsea fans for saying that after the game, but then Xabi Alonso came out and was also heavily critical of the way they had defended - so he and I are on the same page there.

If Joao Pedro is fit then they will at least have more physicality up front this week, but I still have a feeling Leeds will get something out of this.

Daniel Farke's side got a great win over Tottenham last time out and they do not give much away - Arsenal and Brighton are the only top-flight teams to have conceded fewer league goals this season.

Leeds have definitely benefited from signing keeper James Trafford and what a move it has been for him personally as well.

I admire him for that, because he could have hung around at Manchester City as Gianluigi Donnarumma's number two, but he wanted first-team football. Now he is battling it out with Jordan Pickford to be England's number one.

Lauren's prediction: I don't think Leeds will keep Chelsea quiet. 3-1

This is the battle of the Franks... Lampard versus Thomas.

Thomas Frank's first conundrum as Crystal Palace 's new manager is to stop them leaking so many goals - they have conceded 24 in their first 10 games, which is concerning.

I still think Palace have got some really good players, like Ismaila Sarr, Jorgen Strand Larsen and Jean-Philippe Mateta, and it's just a case of them getting fit and finding some form.

The way Coventry play, the Eagles are going to get some chances - but can they take them?

Frank Lampard's side counter-attack with such vigour, so I definitely think they will score... but I can see Palace's forward players having some joy too.

Lauren's prediction: I'm standing next to a Palace fan now, Ed from Boxxer, so I've got to go with them here! 0-2

We've seen Palace change their manager after making a disastrous start but they are still only four points below Ipswich and they will certainly see that as retrievable.

The Tractor Boys are not in the relegation zone but they are still in a relegation fight so, it is important for them to keep picking points up here and there. The trouble for them is that I don't see them getting anything at Tottenham .

Spurs lost to Leeds last time out but I still think they have turned a corner with their performances before that defeat.

I actually think this will be a routine win for Roberto de Zerbi's side, and I'm going for them to keep a clean sheet too.

Lauren's prediction: Spurs will take this one. 2-1

I am covering this game and I think it is a huge one for Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle.

The Magpies have picked up as many points - 12 - in their first 10 games under Jaissle as they did when Eddie Howe was in charge last season, but I still don't think their fans are overly convinced by him.

Some of their unease is because Newcastle don't seem to have a defined style of play, and can be a bit kamikaze going forward.

Because of that, I just think Arsenal will pick them off, and win comfortably.

The Gunners have conceded only five league goals so far and have made an incredible start to their title defence with nine wins out of 10.

The worry for their rivals is that it feels to me Mikel Arteta's side have not even got going yet, but I still don't see anyone being close to them.

Lauren's prediction: No problems for Arsenal here! 0-4

Hull are going to scrap and fight - they have not won for eight games now, but they have still picked up some points because of their battling approach.

You know they will get in Brighton 's faces but I don't think it will bother the Seagulls too much.

I want to apologise to Hull fans because I keep writing the Tigers off every week, but I am going to do it again here because Brighton are such a good team going forward and defensively.

Lauren's prediction: Brighton to edge this one. 0-1

Good luck to Pochettino. I like him as a manager and he seems a decent guy too.

He will need some luck as well, because it is going to be incredibly difficult for him to succeed at Old Trafford.

The constant for Manchester United is their managers keep getting the sack, when the club's problems seem to be deeper-lying than that.

Pochettino will get time because of what he has taken over, but it is amazing and also alarming to think United are in the bottom three, and could be bottom by the time this game is played.

As well as being so poor at the back, they have a midfield without any great athleticism and, stylistically, they did not really have an identity under Michael Carrick.

If you are Pochettino, you are probably going into the dressing room and putting your arm arm around Bruno Fernandes, to get the old sulker onside.

He really needs to, because Fernandes is an outstanding player and played a key role in the club's form with his numbers last season.

United need to see that version of him more than ever now, because so far this season he has not got going at all.

As for Liverpool , well I think they will get there under Andoni Iraola. It is just taking a bit of time for his players to adapt to his style.

They are not particularly fluid most of the time, and it feels like Iraola is not quite sure what his best midfield is.

Liverpool are still a work in progress, and United have picked up some results at Anfield recently - two draws and a win in their past three visits - but I can only see one result here, and it is a home victory.

Pochettino will probably look to defend and play on the counter-attack, and they might get some chances that way, but Liverpool are going to win. The only question is how many they will score.

Carrick began by beating Manchester City and Arsenal in his first two games in January. Pochettino might start by being on the wrong end of a pummelling.

Lauren's prediction: Liverpool are at home and I am going with them to win it. 2-1

Brentford beat Everton 4-2 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium last season but, in three of their past four meetings, the points have been shared.

This has got a draw written all over it, too.

Everton are so solid under David Moyes, and so well organised, that I just don't see them losing. Brentford will keep things tight as well.

Lauren's prediction: Both these teams are doing well and this should be pretty even - I haven't gone for a draw yet, so let's finish with one. 1-1

articles.title: Aberdeen: Mario Frick's first press conference - analysis
articles.summary: Head coach Mario Frick says his track record proves he can produce exciting football - but a back-to-basics approach is needed at Aberdeen.
articles.body:
Aberdeen head coach Mario Frick says his track record proves he can produce exciting football - but for now a back-to-basics approach is required to save the Dons' season.

The 52-year-old arrived in the Granite City on a two-and-a-half year deal earlier this week to replace Stephen Robinson, who was sacked with the team second bottom of the Scottish Premiership.

Frick, who left Luzern in the summer after nearly five years in charge, has already identified a key problem he must solve quickly.

"I am known for high-scoring clubs. Twice with Vaduz we had the highest scoring record and last year with Lucerne, 76 goals," he said.

"I think Aberdeen is lacking goals [12 in 12 league games] so I am here to change that. On Thursday morning for the first time we did our attacking patterns and we have to improve now - we need time but we don't have it.

"More important now is to show the basics - body language, being willing to work, aggression, intensity - that is what I want to see on Saturday in Kilmarnock."

His first game in charge is a real baptism of fire for the Swiss-born former Liechtenstein player.

Defeat for the Dons would mean they replace their Ayrshire hosts at the bottom of the table.

The recent cycle of instability at Aberdeen is highlighted by the fact Frick - who was capped 125 times - has become their seventh permanent manager in six years.

But he is not daunted by recent history or by Aberdeen's situation - and sees similarities between the job he faces at Pittodrie and the one he inherited at Luzern in December 2021.

"I have had a very long career as a professional so I know the pressure. I am always an optimist and I know what I can do," he said.

"Luzern were at the bottom of the table with 18 matches and 11 points and the whole environment was sad and we saved them, so I am pretty sure we can do this also here.

"I am very ambitious. Now it is very important to get out of this situation but we want to go in the top six."

Across almost three decades of working in the north-east of Scotland, I have seen many Aberdeen managers come - and go. In fact, far too many to name check.

From this side of the microphone, first impressions are always intriguing - and not always an accurate barometer for how things will play out.

For example, I watched Neil Warnock cut an impressive figure at his unveiling in February 2024 and look how that worked out.

So what are my early impressions of Mario Frick?

Well, having attended his maiden Pittodrie press conference, and observed him briefly at training this morning at Cormack Park - he exudes a calm authority.

He gives off the vibe of someone who knows where he wants to go, how he wants to get there and I suspect will probably not suffer fools gladly on his way to trying to achieving those ends.

Once both parties get to know each other a bit better, I also get the impression he will quickly command respect from the dressing room.

Frick appears to be a straight talker, and pretty clear in what he wants to get across.

While that obviously bodes well from a journalist's point of view, more importantly it could be crucial for the players as he looks to quickly deliver a winning formula that he, and the fans, hope can get the team moving back up the Premiership table over the coming months.

"With a manager change there is still a chance for every player to prove themselves, a new chance for everybody.

"To be honest I was really surprised with the first training session. It was brilliant and I saw a lot of quality.

"The facilities are paradise, it is incredible. It is better than in Switzerland so for me it is the next step. I am very happy to be here. I am very thankful to Adrian [Bevington, chief executive], Lutz [Pfannenstiel, sporting director], Mr Cormack [Dave, chairman], and the whole board."

"For eight years I have been a professional coach with only two clubs.

"Then I felt it is time for the next step. I waited for five months for this next step and when Lutz called me on Monday after the Hibs game I was excited from the first moment.

"I am really, really happy to be here because it is such a big club, such a famous club, a historic club, I am just proud to be here."

"Heavy metal, that is high-pressing, that is counter-pressing, vertical play, creating many goalscoring chances, that is heavy metal.

"In the next two weeks we have five games so I am just getting to know the new team and I have to make some very difficult decisions. But I am an optimist and I think we can do very well."

articles.title: Vitor Matos: Swansea 'acknowledge' head coach move to Strasbourg
articles.summary: Swansea City belatedly confirm that boss Vitor Matos has left the Championship club by saying only that they "acknowledge" Strasbourg's statement over his move to the French club.
articles.body:
Swansea City have belatedly confirmed that head coach Vitor Matos has left the Championship club by saying only that they "acknowledge" Strasbourg's statement over his move to the French side.

Strasbourg announced the appointment of Matos as their new boss on Wednesday evening.

Around 23 hours later, Swansea issued a statement of their own featuring only one line on Matos.

"Per RC Strasbourg's announcement, Swansea City acknowledges that Vitor Matos and his coaching staff have left the club," the Welsh club said.

Swansea's statement initially misspelled Matos' first name, as Victor rather than Vitor. The same error was made in Strasbourg's English language social media announcement of his appointment on Wednesday.

The 'mistake' was quickly updated on the Swansea's website. When asked whether the misspelling had been deliberate, a Swansea spokesperson declined to comment.

Swansea say former captain Ashley Williams will lead a temporary coaching team tasked with filling the void left by Matos' departure.

"Swansea City can confirm club greats Ashley Williams, Leon Britton, Joe Allen and Kris O'Leary – a quartet boasting over 1,400 appearances in black and white – will be at the helm for Saturday's game against West Bromwich Albion," the club's statement added.

"Additionally, head of academy goalkeeping Paul Whitfield has stepped up to the senior set-up, with the group taking today's (Thursday) training session at Fairwood.

"The club wants to place on record its thanks to Ashley, Leon, Joe, Kris and Paul for making themselves immediately available without hesitation, and we are grateful to have people with such a great passion for Swansea City guiding us through this period."

Strasbourg are expected to pay Swansea a compensation fee thought to be in the region of £5m for Matos, who has left despite agreeing a new contract running until 2030 in July.

The 38-year-old spent just under a year at Swansea, having left his role as Maritimo boss - after only 12 games in charge - to succeed Alan Sheehan as the Championship club's head coach in November 2025.

Four members of Matos' coaching team - Diogo Medeiros, Toze Mendes, Goncalo Ricca and head of goalkeeping Pedro Pereira - are also expected to leave Swansea.

A badly timed shock - the story of Matos' Swans exit

Latest Swansea City news, analysis and fan views

Listen to the latest Swansea City interviews, news and discussion on BBC Sounds

Allen and Williams return to the club to join an interim coaching team alongside fellow former players O'Leary and Britton.

O'Leary and Britton are the only remaining members of Matos' backroom staff, with academy goalkeeping coach Paul Whitfield temporarily stepping up to first-team level.

The hastily assembled coaching group will lead Swansea while the club searches for Matos' permanent successor, with their first game in charge coming when West Bromwich Albion visit on Saturday.

Swansea then go to Middlesbrough next Tuesday before hosting Welsh rivals Cardiff City on Sunday, 29 November.

"Our focus is firmly on this weekend's fixture against West Bromwich Albion and collectively working to continue to drive the club forward," the Swans' statement added.

Analysis: A sorry end to a reign which promised much

Swansea's long-awaited statement on Vitor Matos' exit – or should we say Victor – is about as cold as they come.

The Welsh club are unhappy over various aspects of Matos' move to France.

Without saying as much, they have made that abundantly clear.

Barely a week ago, Matos was his usual chirpy self at Swansea's Fairwood training base, as he chatted to BBC Sport Wales about Marko Stamenic's three-match suspension and which of his injured players might be fit to play against West Bromwich Albion this Saturday.

By last weekend, Strasbourg had made their move for the Swansea head coach – and suddenly Matos' plans for West Brom were forgotten.

His surprise departure all happened very swiftly and, as Swansea's statement shows, has left a sour taste for many within the club.

The wait for the Swans to say anything was not a result of bitterness towards Matos.

BBC Sport Wales understands the Championship side - unusually in this sort of situation - did not know Strasbourg's announcement was coming on Wednesday, and they were particularly surprised when it did given that they did not believe the process of finalising Matos' move had been completed.

It all amounts to a sorry end to a reign which brought plenty of progress, and had promised much more.

articles.title: Michigan WR Andrew Marsh facing indecent exposure charge for allegedly exposing himself to delivery driver
articles.summary: Marsh leads Michigan with 48 catches in 2026. He was charged in October over the February allegation.
articles.body:
Michigan wide receiver Andrew Marsh is facing a misdemeanor indecent exposure charge after a food delivery driver said he exposed himself to her after she dropped off food at his residence on Feb. 2, 2026.

According to a release from the Pittsfield Township Police Department that does not mention Marsh by name, the delivery driver said "the door was answered by a male subject with a blanket draped over his shoulders. The complainant reported that the subject was unclothed beneath the blanket. As she turned to leave, the male subject pulled the blanket apart, exposing his genitals."

The driver then stated that she "left the residence and subsequently received a message from the customer stating that she was attractive and asking if she would return to the address."

The Detroit News confirmed that Marsh's residence is located on the street identified in the release.

Online court records show that Marsh has a hearing on Dec. 2 and was officially charged on Oct. 14. Michigan said in a statement it was "made aware of an incident involving Andrew Marsh" and it would "continue to monitor the situation as more information becomes available, but we are unable to comment further due to the on-going case."

Marsh was listed as questionable on Michigan's Wednesday night availability report and MLive reported he did not appear for a previously scheduled media availability on Tuesday.

Marsh, a sophomore, leads Michigan with 48 catches and is second on the team with 459 receiving yards. He's one of just three players with a receiving touchdown this season. The former four-star recruit had 45 catches for 651 yards and four touchdowns as a freshman in 2025 while the Wolverines went 9-4. This season, Michigan is 5-5 and needs a win over either No. 4 UCLA or No. 14 Ohio State to make a bowl game.

articles.title: Thomas Frank: Crystal Palace boss happy to be 'back in the circus'
articles.summary: Thomas Frank is happy to be "back in the circus" after speaking at his first news conference as Crystal Palace manager.
articles.body:
Thomas Frank is happy to be "back in the circus" after speaking at his first news conference as Crystal Palace manager.

The 53-year-old, who was appointed on a two-and-a-half-year deal on Monday, has been out of worked since he was sacked by Tottenham in February, less than eight months after taking the job.

But, rather than dwell on that disappointment, Frank hopes to use it as a learning exeprience as he attempts to improve Palace's fortunes and lift them off the bottom of the Premier League table.

"If you don't learn from any of your jobs, I don't think you reflect, I don't think you improve, and I don't think you get better," said Frank.

"Of course there's a lot of things I have been reflecting over. The details, that will be for another time, but I can say I've learned, definitely."

The Dane said he could easily have extended his break from football, which he used to travel to Japan and Australia, as well as "visiting friends and family, eating too well [and] drinking too much wine" back in his homeland.

"I was very aware I didn't want to do anything in the summer. I put a statement out there, I needed more time," he added.

"I can actually, honestly say I would have been fine if it was three, four, five, six, seven months more, because it's good to be back in the circus, but it's also unbelievably good not to be in, especially if you enjoy life, which I do.

"I was spending time with family and friends and doing all that, but I think the club, the way Palace is, how well Steve Parish especially spoke about the club and ideas, Matt Hobbs and Iain Moody and these guys, too, helped convince me it was a good idea.

"I'm a little bit surprised by this feeling I have in the body, how good it feels."

How Frank can restore reputation and save Crystal Palace

Frank's Palace reign begins with a trip to Coventry City on Saturday (15:00 GMT) and he says he returns to the dugout unbruised despite the way his stint at Spurs ended.

"I think we all have an ego," the former Brentford boss said. "Some are better at controlling it than others. For me, it's not the critics, it's more what I can learn, what I can prove, how I can get better.

"There's a lot of clever people out there, but the interesting thing is they only know 10 per cent of the truth. That's a tenth of the truth at Brentford , there's a tenth of the truth at Tottenham , and that's just the way it is.

"If you can't handle that as a coach or a player, then you shouldn't be in this business, and I'm very happy to be back in the game."

articles.body: El Rayo Vallecano y su afición siguen acercando posturas. La Federación de Peñas del Rayo Vallecano ha hecho público un nuevo comunicado en el que anuncian importantes novedades y acuerdos que se han alcanzado gracias a las reuniones entre los representantes de las peñas y del club. En este caso, ha sido la segunda, después de la que tuvo lugar durante el mes de octubre. De acuerdo con el comunicado, el club se compromete a "fomentar la creación de nuevas peñas rayistas renovando la normativa interna", a lanzar un comunicado anunciando "todos los detalles sobre la devolución de la parte proporcional del abono por los partidos no disputados esta temporada en el Estadio de Vallecas", el próximo viernes día 20, y a "colaborar con los actos solidarios de las peñas rayistas". Por otra parte, se sigue negociando sobre el precio de los abonos de las próximas temporadas, la forma de gestionar las entradas (tanto visitantes como la creación de una plataforma para la venta online), el fin del veto a medios de comunicación ligados al Rayo y sobre el futuro del Estadio de Vallecas. "Celebramos que, más de una década después, la directiva del Club esté dispuesta a sentarse de nuevo con sus aficionados y trabajar conjuntamente con ellos por el bien del Rayo Vallecano y de Vallecas, sin olvidarnos de todos los problemas que nos han traído hasta aquí", relata el comunicado. Por último, las Peñas comunican que están abiertas a "recibir cualquier propuesta de la afición y dispuestos a trabajar en ellas, con el objetivo de concretar poco a poco estos y el resto de asuntos que no se han podido cerrar en las dos reuniones iniciales".

articles.title: Report: Saints, 143-game veteran to 'discuss his future with the team'
articles.summary: Saints GM Mickey Loomis will have a hard time getting out of lackluster DB Justin Reid's contract after failing to move him at the NFL trade deadline.
articles.body:
Here's something. Veteran safety Justin Reid is taking this week to "discuss his future with" the New Orleans Saints , per NewOrleans.Football's Nick Underhill . Ironically, it's been a year to the day since wide receiver Brandin Cooks was listed on the injury report for "personal reasons" and asked for his release, which was granted a few days later. Reid had the same designation on Wednesday .

The two players found themselves in similar situations. Both Cooks and Reid were some of the first big investments Kellen Moore made in free agency, but they each found the reality of their new team to be lacking. Cooks wasn't happy with how few targets he was seeing, and that a younger quarterback than Derek Carr was the one throwing them (in other words, he felt like this wasn't what he signed up for).

It's less clear what Reid has to gripe about. He was named a team captain in 2025 and played almost 100% of snaps in every game when healthy, at least until recently. He suffered a concussion against the Pittsburgh Steelers and returned to see 76.7% and 78.6% of snaps during the next two games. He's had a starting role in the defense but has delivered with impact plays. Reid only has one takeaway in 24 games with New Orleans while missing 22 tackles, per Pro Football Focus charting.

What's disappointing is that the Saints failed to trade either Reid or Cooks when they had the chance at the NFL deadline. Instead of taking offers on the table for Cooks, he was let go and left behind $3.2 million in dead money on this year's books. Cutting Reid ( who we know teams were interested in ) would leave $13.26 million on the 2027 salary cap, up from his current cap hit of $13.14 million. That's because the Saints restructured his contract earlier this year. They expected Reid would be a positive influence on his less-experienced teammates, lead the defense, and be someone they could count on. That hasn't been the case. We'll see if the situation changes and whether Reid is let go -- and what he would have to give back, if anything, to make it happen.

articles.title: Two PGA TOUR Spots Loom For Walker Cup Teammates
articles.summary: Walker Cup teammates return to the Bahamas for a high-stakes playoff. Two PGA TOUR exemptions hang in the balance at the ITG Tournament of Champions.
articles.body:
Amateur golf rarely offers a prize this sweet, yet the ITG Tournament of Champions is about to hand out two full PGA TOUR starts. Between December 14 and December 16, 2026, the Ocean Club Golf Course on Paradise Island will host an event that offers rewards exceeding a gold medal. Grayson Wood already secured one of these golden tickets by winning the inaugural event last December, but the second spot remains wide open for the current field.

Tyler Watts, Miles Russell, and Kihei Akina are the names to watch as they return to the Bahamas to chase that elusive second exemption. The tournament structure creates a unique pressure cooker where the runner-up finish carries real weight. According to AmateurGolf.com , the Myrtle Beach Classic and the Puerto Rico Open are the specific events on offer for the champion and the runner-up. This setup forces elite amateurs to treat every shot with the intensity of a major championship final round.

History shows just how much the second spot matters when the leaderboard tightens. Last year, Grayson Wood shot an 8-under 208 to claim his prize, leaving a group of four players tied at 7-under 209. That tie triggered a four-for-one playoff for the remaining exemption, turning a standard amateur tournament into a do-or-die battle. North Carolina's Carson Bertagnole was one of those players who had to fight for his spot. He made two crucial pars to stay alive alongside Tyler Kowack, eventually securing the opportunity.

When tournament media asked if he knew about the event offering two PGA TOUR spots, he gave a short, grounded answer. "No. But I'm not going to complain," Bertagnole told tournament media. That line sums up the mindset required here. The players know the odds are stacked against them, yet the reward is too big to ignore.

The tournament organizers have designed a format that guarantees tension right until the final putt drops. Beginning with a 36-hole competition day and concluding with an 18-hole final round, the tournament comprises 54 holes of stroke play. Ocean Club, a Tom Weiskopf design, plays as a par 72 stretching 7,159 yards. The champion and the runner-up will receive the two sponsor exemptions, making every hole on the final day a direct path to the professional ranks. According to AmateurGolf.com, the White Sands Bahamas Men's Invitational first appeared in 2025 utilizing its individual amateur format.

In 2025, the first individual edition drew 19 players from the global top 100 and secured the ninth spot among men's amateur tournaments via WAGR rating. Those figures are the organizer's reported assessment, but the results speak for themselves.

Walker Cup teammates head back to the ITG Tournament of Champions from December 14–16, 2026, where two PGA TOUR starts are on offer.

articles.title: Rumor Claims Cody Rhodes Heel Turn Faces Major Internal Hurdle
articles.summary: Fans hoping to see a heel Cody Rhodes may have to keep waiting. WrestleVotes reported on WrestleVotes Radio for Fightful […]
articles.body:
Fans hoping to see a heel Cody Rhodes may have to keep waiting. WrestleVotes reported on WrestleVotes Radio for Fightful Select that at least several important figures at TKO are firmly against Rhodes turning heel, whatever it might do for his storylines.

Within TKO, Rhodes is seen as the model good guy and a loyal company man. His merchandise sales and big-name sponsorship deals are a big part of that, and TKO does not want to put them at risk at this time. The source said a turn might make for good TV, but the people in charge do not think it is worth the price at this time.

The report follows Rhodes' own comments on the subject. In an interview with UnSportsmanlike, which Fightful reported last week, Rhodes was asked about turning heel and joining forces with Paul Heyman .

"I think it looks different than people think," Rhodes said. He added that "if you think I'm a heel, then I'm already a heel."

Rhodes said he was "very open to it" but that the decision belongs to WWE. "But if it's never time, I'm sorry. I don't know," he said.

Talk of a Rhodes heel turn has followed him for much of his second WWE run. Speculation picked up after he lost the Undisputed WWE Championship to Drew McIntyre in January, and it resurfaced in August when he borrowed Heyman's catchphrase, "That is not a prediction, it's a spoiler," during a promo with Randy Orton on SmackDown.

Rhodes is set to captain Team USA against Team Mexico at next week's Survivor Series: WarGames in Houston. His team includes CM Punk, Je'Von Evans and LA Knight, with one spot open. Rhodes won the title back from McIntyre in March before losing it to Sami Zayn at Night of Champions in June, and Zayn holds the championship heading into Survivor Series.

The Rock will also be in Houston. The two have history, from The Rock pinning Rhodes at WrestleMania 40 to demanding his soul at Elimination Chamber 2025, a story that ended when Rhodes refused and John Cena turned on him.

A heel turn for Rhodes would make headlines, but TKO's position makes sense. Rhodes is a central figure for WWE's business side. He is the guy on the merchandise tables, in marketing campaigns and at the center of the company's biggest shows. Turning him into a heel would put all of that at risk for a storyline payoff that may not last.

There are also better ways to keep him interesting. Rhodes can show more of an edge without crossing over, and The Rock's appearance in Houston gives WWE a ready-made foil who brings out that side of him. A babyface Rhodes chasing the title and standing up to The Rock is a story that writes itself.

The heel turn will stay on the table as long as Rhodes keeps talking about it, but the people who sign off on the big decisions reportedly are not on board. Until that changes, the American Nightmare is staying on the right side of the line.

articles.title: Iago Machado, of Brazil U17s, on his first World Cup and title hopes
articles.summary: Iago Machado highlighted the squad’s unityCredits: Nelson Terme /CBFA first World Cup is now a reality for Iago Machado. Called up to represent Brazil’s men’...
articles.body:
Iago Machado highlighted the squad's unity Credits: Nelson Terme /CBF

A first World Cup is now a reality for Iago Machado. Called up to represent Brazil's men's U-17 national team in Qatar, the Corinthians player spoke about fulfilling his dream of playing in the tournament, preparations for the clash with Ireland and the importance of the unity the squad has built over recent months.

"First of all, it's an honor to be taking part in my first World Cup, especially alongside great players from great clubs. I can only thank God, my family and the coaching staff for this opportunity. Hopefully we can have a fantastic tournament and lift this trophy for Brazil," he said.

Brazil heads into its tournament opener after a period of preparation and analysis of its opponents. Iago said the team has studied Ireland's characteristics to find ways to impose its own style of play.

"We've been preparing really well, studying Ireland's strengths and looking at their strong and weak points so we can play our own game. I hope we have a great match, a great debut and, God willing, come away proud of a victory," he said.

The defender also spoke about his relationship with his teammates and the importance of close bonds between the players in strengthening the team. Some members of the squad already knew each other from previous call-ups, which he said helped them settle in quickly.

"I'd known some of them for quite a while, so it was very easy to settle in with them. The unity we have, being together since the warm-up matches, has been really important and really constructive for a competition as important as the World Cup," he said.

Iago also spoke about what fans can expect from his performances during the tournament. Focused and ready to make the most of his opportunities, he emphasized his team spirit and commitment to helping the squad grow throughout the competition.

"You can expect someone who is very focused, ready for every opportunity that comes his way, and a team player who helps others so this squad can grow and win titles," he concluded.

Brazil's men's U-17 national team makes its World Cup debut this Saturday (21) against Ireland at 6 p.m. local time (noon Brasília time) at Aspire Zone in Doha. Brazil is in Group I, which also includes Costa Rica and Tanzania.

articles.title: MC&J: Ohio State hits the road for the final time in the regular season in Week 12
articles.summary: Much like Ohio State, Brett will be looking to build off a positive performance last week. With one weekend left before The Game, he has spread picks for Buc...
articles.body:
Last week ATS: 11-8 (7-3 National, 4-5 B1G)

Season ATS: 103-100 (44-43 National, 59-57 B1G)

Last week was a bit of a struggle, but at least we ended the week with a record above .500.

Ohio State didn't help things by choking away a cover late in the game, but some later in the night Iowa stood strong in the red zone to preserve a cover against Purdue. You win some, you lose some.

After this week we have just one week of the regular season left, followed by the final conference championship weekend. It would definitely boost morale heading into Thanksgiving if we were able to put some more distance on the .500 mark.

Hopefully we are on the right side of a lot of these predictions.

LSU (-1.5) v. No. 9 Tennessee – 3:30 p.m. ET – ABC

Even though this isn't the first time Lane Kiffin has taken on the Vols in Knoxville since leaving Tennessee for USC years ago, the former head coach of the Volunteers can get a bit of payback for the scene in 2021 in Knoxville when fans threw debris on the field.

With a win on Saturday, LSU can put a dent into the playoff hopes of Tennessee.

The defense of the Volunteers has been tough to crack this year, not allowing more than 24 points in a game this year. Already Tennessee has taken down Alabama and Kentucky in Knoxville this year. Josh Heupel has needed his defense to come up big since the Vols don't have a quarterback who has thrown for 1,000 yards so far this season.

LSU will likely come in playing loose since they have nothing to lose after last week's loss to Texas. It's unlikely the Tigers will make the CFP now that they have four losses.

As long as Sam Leavitt doesn't turn the football over, LSU has a great shot at playing spoiler.

No. 12 Texas Tech (-3.5) v. Baylor – 3:30 p.m. ET – FOX

After suffering their only loss of the season to Cincinnati last month, Texas Tech has responded with three straight wins.

In their last two games, the Red Raiders have put up a combined 105 points in wins over West Virginia and Oklahoma State. In those two victories, quarterback Thomas Castellanos has been hitting a bunch of big plays through the air, totaling over 600 yards on just 30 completions.

Baylor fired head coach Dave Aranda near the end of October and responded with wins over UCF and Iowa State before losing in Provo last week to BYU. DJ Lagway has been pretty good at quarterback but the Bears have struggled to run the football, totaling 1,480 yards on the ground as a team.

Even though Baylor will be at home and looking to end the playoff hopes of Texas Tech, the Bears just aren't on the same level as the Red Raiders.

If Texas Tech can go into Stillwater and easily handle Oklahoma State, I don't see why they can't do the same to Baylor at their place.

No. 2 Utah (-6.5) v. TCU – 9:00 p.m. ET – FOX

Utah won a thriller late last week in Tucson, taking down Arizona 40-39.

Running back Wayshawn Parker was limited to just one carry, leaving Daniel Bray to almost double his season total on the ground, rushing for 197 yards against the Wildcats. The Utes can get it done both on the ground and through the air with Devon Dampier at quarterback.

TCU has had a hard time gaining any traction this season. Over the last five games the Horned Frogs have alternated wins and losses. If that trend continues, TCU is due for a loss this week after beating Kansas State 20-10. Offense has been limited for the Horned Frogs, as the last time they reached 30 points in a game was when they beat Arkansas State 31-7.

The Utes shouldn't have nearly as much trouble with TCU this week as they did with Arizona last Saturday. The Horned Frogs don't have the look of a team who could spring an upset of this magnitude.

Being so close to an undefeated regular season, as well as a spot in the College Football Playoff, it's hard to see Utah falling this week.

No. 14 Ohio State (-3.5) v. Nebraska – 12:00 p.m. ET – FOX

Will Ohio State's win last week create enough momentum to allow the Buckeyes to win their final two regular season games? Can Ohio State get enough help to make the Big Ten Championship Game and possibly earn a spot in the College Football Playoff?

A lot will be on the line for the Buckeyes on Saturday when they head to Lincoln to take on Nebraska.

Ohio State is going to probably need a miracle to make it to Indianapolis next month. Essentially the Buckeyes need Washington to beat both Indiana and Oregon in the next two weeks to have a shot at making it to the Big Ten Championship Game for the second straight season.

At least a spot in the College Football Playoff seems a little more reachable.

Last week the Buckeyes got back to what they do best. Getting the football to Jeremiah Smith. The junior wide receiver now has back-to-back 100-yard games. The chemistry between Smith and Luke Fahey seems to be getting strong with each start the freshman quarterback makes.

Nebraska started off the season hot with a 5-0 start, but then proceeded to drop four games in a row before shutting out Rutgers last week. In true Cornhusker fashion, those losses were heartbreaking because of how close they all were, as the four defeats were by a combined 24 points.

If Nebraska is ever able to figure out how to win a close conference game then they might be able to return to the glory we saw from the program under Tom Osborne.

The Buckeyes have dominated the series with the Cornhuskers, winning 10 of 11 meetings. The only time Nebraska beat Ohio State came in Lincoln in 2011 when Luke Fickell was the interim head coach of the Buckeyes.

Even though Ohio State isn't quite as dangerous without Julian Sayin at quarterback, the Buckeyes should be able to win their second game in a row and head into The Game with some momentum.

No. 4 UCLA (-3.5) v. Michigan – 3:30 p.m. ET – CBS

If you were going to compare Bob Chesney's first year at UCLA to Curt Cignetti's first year at Indiana, this is the week the clock strikes midnight for the Bruins.

Back in 2024, Indiana suffered their first loss under Cignetti in their 11th game of the regular season when they lost to Ohio State. UCLA enters this week's game at 10-0 and hit the road to take on Michigan.

Luckily for UCLA, Michigan isn't the same kind of monster Ohio State was in 2024. The Wolverines have scored a combined 15 points over their last two games. Apparently the honeymoon with Tommy Carr at quarterback is over.

If it wasn't for the defense then the Wolverines would be an even bigger mess.

The Bruins could send Michigan to Columbus next week needing a win just to become bowl eligible. Quarterback Ty Dieffenbach makes the right decisions when he is called on, which isn't that much since UCLA is great at running the football and controlling the clock.

The Bruins head into next week's showdown with USC without a blemish on their record.

No. 8 Indiana (-8.5) v. Washington – 3:30 p.m. ET – Peacock

This has been a disappointing season for Washington. The Huskies thought they might be a factor in the College Football Playoff race after a solid 2025 season.

Following last week's 21-14 win at Michigan State, Washington is just 6-4 on the season. Now the only way they can have an impact on the CFP is if they beat Indiana and add to the chaos we have seen recently.

The Hoosiers haven't exactly been crisp lately. Following their loss to Ohio State, Indiana needed overtime to beat Michigan and Minnesota. Last week the Hoosiers were tied with USC in the third quarter before creating some distance with two touchdowns. Josh Hoover has been dinged up, leaving Grant Wilson to take the snaps last week.

Going to Seattle is never an easy trip. I'm not saying I think the Huskies are going to beat Indiana, but they are going to make things tough for Curt Cignetti's team.

I feel like this is the kind of game that doesn't get decided until late in the fourth quarter.
